bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通-{鑑}-巻第二百一十六

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 216.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 216.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀三十二】起強圉大淵獻十二月，盡昭陽大荒落，凡六年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 32:] From the twelfth month of the year Qiangyu Dayuanxian through the year Zhaoyang Dahuangluo, altogether six years and a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Records 32 spans from the twelfth month of the year Qiangyu Dayuanxian through the year Zhaoyang Dahuangluo—a period of just over six years.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己巳，上以仙芝爲安西四鎭節度使，-{-{征}-}-靈察入朝，靈察大懼。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jisi, the emperor appointed Xianzhi as military commissioner of the four Anxi garrisons and summoned Lingcha to court; Lingcha was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day jisi, the emperor named Gao Xianzhi military commissioner of the four Anxi garrisons and recalled Fumeng Lingcha to the capital. Lingcha was terrified.

sentences.zh: 仙芝見靈察，趨走如故，靈察益懼。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi saw Lingcha, he hurried forward as before; Lingcha grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi met Lingcha, he rushed to greet him just as he always had, which only deepened Lingcha's fear.

sentences.zh: 副都護京兆程千-{里}-、押牙畢思琛及行官王滔等，皆平日構仙芝-{於}-靈察者也，仙芝-{面}-責千-{里}-、思琛曰：「公-{面}-雖男子，心如婦人，何也？」

translations.literal: The vice protector-general Cheng Qianli of Jingzhao, the yaya Bi Sichen, and the staff officer Wang Tao and others had all in ordinary times slandered Xianzhi to Lingcha. Xianzhi rebuked Qianli and Sichen to their faces, saying, "Your faces are those of men, yet your hearts are like women's—how is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Vice protector-general Cheng Qianli of Jingzhao, the yaya Bi Sichen, and the staff officer Wang Tao had all routinely maligned Xianzhi to Lingcha. Xianzhi confronted Qianli and Sichen and said, "You look like men, yet you have the hearts of women—how can that be?"

sentences.zh: 又捽滔等，欲笞之，既而皆釋之，謂曰：「吾素所恨-{於}-汝者，欲不言，恐汝懷憂；

translations.literal: He then seized Tao and the others and was about to flog them, but afterward released them all and said, "What I have long resented in you I wished not to speak of, fearing you would brood in anxiety;
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Wang Tao and the others and was about to have them beaten, but in the end let them all go. He told them, "The grievances I have long held against you I kept silent about, lest you worry yourselves sick;

sentences.zh: 今既言之，則無事矣。」

translations.literal: now that I have spoken, there is nothing more to it."
translations.idiomatic: now that I have said it plainly, the matter is finished."

sentences.zh: 軍中乃安。

translations.literal: The army thereupon settled down.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the army was reassured.

sentences.zh: 初，仙芝爲都知兵馬使，猗氏人封常淸，少孤貧，細瘦纇目，一足偏短，求爲仙芝傔，不納。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xianzhi was director of military affairs, Feng Changqing of Yishi, orphaned and poor in youth, slight and thin with sunken eyes and one leg somewhat short, asked to serve as Xianzhi's attendant and was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Xianzhi was director of military affairs, Feng Changqing of Yishi—orphaned and poor as a youth, slight and gaunt with sunken eyes and one leg shorter than the other—asked to serve as his attendant, but Xianzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 常淸日候仙芝出入，不離其門，凡數十日，仙芝不得已留之。

translations.literal: Changqing daily waited on Xianzhi's comings and goings and never left his gate; after several tens of days, Xianzhi had no choice but to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing waited at Xianzhi's door every day, never leaving his post. After several weeks, Xianzhi reluctantly took him on.

sentences.zh: 會達奚部叛走，夫蒙靈察使仙芝追之，斬獲略盡。

translations.literal: It happened that the Daxi tribe rebelled and fled; Fumeng Lingcha sent Xianzhi in pursuit, and he killed and captured nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Daxi tribe rebelled and fled, Fumeng Lingcha sent Xianzhi in pursuit. Xianzhi killed or captured nearly the entire force.

sentences.zh: 常淸私作捷書以示仙芝，皆仙芝心所欲言者，由是一府奇之。

translations.literal: Changqing privately drafted a victory report and showed it to Xianzhi; everything in it was what Xianzhi wished to say in his heart, and from this the whole headquarters regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing privately drafted a victory dispatch and showed it to Xianzhi. Every line expressed exactly what Xianzhi had wanted to say, and from that day the whole headquarters regarded him as remarkable.

sentences.zh: 仙芝爲節度使，即署常淸判官；

translations.literal: When Xianzhi became military commissioner, he immediately appointed Changqing as his adjutant;
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi became military commissioner, he immediately appointed Changqing adjutant;

translations.literal: whenever Xianzhi went on campaign, Changqing regularly served as rear commander.
translations.idiomatic: whenever Xianzhi marched out on campaign, Changqing remained behind as rear commander.

sentences.zh: 仙芝乳母子鄭德詮爲郎將，仙芝遇之如兄弟，使典家事，威行軍中。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's foster brother Zheng Dexuan served as a langjiang; Xianzhi treated him like a brother, put him in charge of household affairs, and his authority prevailed throughout the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's foster brother Zheng Dexuan held the rank of langjiang. Xianzhi treated him like a brother, entrusted him with household affairs, and his authority ran throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 常淸嘗出，德詮走馬自-{後}-突之而過。

translations.literal: Once when Changqing went out, Dexuan galloped from behind and brushed past him.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Changqing was out riding, Dexuan galloped up from behind and shouldered past him.

sentences.zh: 常淸至使院，使召德詮，毎過一門，輒闔之，既至，常淸離度謂曰：「常淸本出寒微，郎將所知。

translations.literal: Changqing returned to the commissionerate, sent for Dexuan, and each time he passed through a gate had it shut behind him. When Dexuan arrived, Changqing said with composure, "Changqing was originally of humble birth, as the langjiang knows.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing returned to headquarters and sent for Dexuan, ordering each gate shut behind him as he passed. When Dexuan arrived, Changqing said calmly, "You know that I come from humble origins.

sentences.zh: 今日中丞命爲留-{後}-，郎將何得-{於}-衆中相陵突！」

translations.literal: Today the commissioner has ordered me to serve as rear commander—how can the langjiang bully and insult me before the assembled troops!"
translations.idiomatic: Today the commissioner has appointed me rear commander. How dare you ride down a fellow officer in front of the whole army!"

sentences.zh: 因叱之曰：「郎將須暫死以肅軍政！」

translations.literal: He then shouted at him, "The langjiang must die for a moment to restore military discipline!"
translations.idiomatic: He shouted, "You will have to die for a moment, langjiang, if army discipline is to be upheld!"

sentences.zh: 遂杖之六十，-{面}--{仆}-地曳出。

translations.literal: He then had him beaten sixty strokes and dragged out face down along the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He had him beaten sixty strokes and dragged out facedown along the ground.

sentences.zh: 仙芝妻及乳母-{於}-門外叫哭救之，不及，因以狀白仙芝。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's wife and foster mother cried out at the gate to save him but were too late; they therefore reported the matter to Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's wife and foster mother wailed at the gate to save him, but it was too late. They reported what had happened to Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 仙芝覽之，驚曰：「已死邪？」

translations.literal: Xianzhi read the report and said in alarm, "Is he already dead?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi read the report and exclaimed in alarm, "Is he dead already?"

sentences.zh: 及見常淸，遂不-{復}-言，常淸亦不之謝。

translations.literal: When he saw Changqing, he said no more, and Changqing did not thank him either.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Changqing, he said nothing more, and Changqing offered no apology either.

sentences.zh: 軍中畏之惕息。

translations.literal: Throughout the army they feared him and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army feared him and dared not breathe freely.

sentences.zh: 自唐興以來，邊帥皆用忠厚名臣，不久任，不遙領，不兼統，功名著者往往入爲宰相。

translations.literal: Since the rise of Tang, frontier commanders were all loyal and substantial famous ministers; they did not hold office long, did not hold distant commissions, and did not combine several commands. Those whose merit was illustrious often entered the government as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the Tang, frontier commanders had been drawn from loyal, eminent statesmen. Their terms were short; they did not hold distant commissions or combine several commands at once. Those who distinguished themselves were often recalled to serve as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 其四夷之將，雖-{才}-略如阿史那社爾、契苾何力猶不專大將之任，皆以大臣爲使以-{制}-之。

translations.literal: Even for generals from the four barbarian groups, though their talent and strategy were like Ashina She'er's or Qibi Heli's, they still did not hold the chief command exclusively; all were placed under civil ministers sent as commissioners to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Even foreign generals as capable as Ashina She'er or Qibi Heli did not hold sole command. A civil minister was always sent to supervise them.

sentences.zh: 及開元中，天子有呑四夷之-{志}-，爲邊將者十-{餘}-年不易，始久任矣；

translations.literal: By the Kaiyuan era the Son of Heaven had the ambition to swallow the four barbarians; frontier generals went more than ten years without being replaced, and long tenure began;
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era the emperor set out to subdue the border peoples, and frontier generals began to hold their posts for ten years or more without rotation;

sentences.zh: 皇子則慶、忠諸王，宰相則蕭-{嵩}-、牛仙客，始遙領矣；

translations.literal: among princes such as the Kings of Qing and Zhong, and among chief ministers such as Xiao Song and Niu Xianke, distant commissions began;
translations.idiomatic: princes such as the Kings of Qing and Zhong, and chief ministers such as Xiao Song and Niu Xianke, began to hold commissions in name only from afar;

sentences.zh: 蓋嘉運、王忠嗣專-{制}-數道，始兼統矣。

translations.literal: Gai Jiayun and Wang Zhongsi monopolized several circuits, and combined command began.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Jiayun and Wang Zhongsi came to dominate several circuits, and the practice of holding multiple commands began.

sentences.zh: 李林甫欲杜邊帥入相之路，以胡人不知書，乃奏言：「文臣爲將，怯當矢石，不若用寒畯胡人；

translations.literal: Li Linfu wished to block the path by which frontier commanders entered the chancellorship. Because barbarians did not know books, he memorialized, saying, "When civil officials serve as generals, they are timid before arrows and stones; it is better to use humble barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu wanted to shut frontier commanders out of the chancellorship. Because non-Chinese officers were unlettered, he argued, "Civil officials make poor generals—they flinch at arrows and stones. Better to appoint humble barbarian officers;

sentences.zh: 胡人則勇決習戰，寒族則孤立無黨，陛下誠心恩洽其心，彼必能爲朝廷盡死。」

translations.literal: barbarians are brave, resolute, and practiced in war; men of humble clans stand alone without factions. If Your Majesty sincerely treats their hearts with grace, they will surely die to the utmost for the court."
translations.idiomatic: barbarians are bold, decisive, and skilled in war; men from poor families stand alone without political ties. If Your Majesty wins their hearts with genuine favor, they will fight to the death for the throne."

sentences.zh: 上悅其言，始用安祿山。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased with this advice and first employed An Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with this advice and first elevated An Lushan.

sentences.zh: 至是，諸道節度使盡用胡人，精兵-{鹹}-戍北邊，天下之勢偏重，卒使祿山傾覆天下，皆出-{於}-林甫專寵固位之謀也。

translations.literal: By this time military commissioners of every circuit were all barbarians; elite troops were all garrisoned on the northern frontier; the weight of empire tilted to one side; and in the end Lushan overturned the realm—all arising from Li Linfu's scheme to monopolize favor and secure his position.
translations.idiomatic: By then every circuit commissioner was a non-Chinese officer, and the empire's best troops were massed on the northern frontier. The balance of power shifted dangerously northward, and in the end An Lushan overturned the realm—all of it the fruit of Li Linfu's plot to hoard favor and cling to office.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛-{丑}-，左監門大將軍、知内侍省事髙力士加驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day xinchou, the Left Gate Guard General and director of palace eunuch affairs Gao Lishi was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day xinchou, Gao Lishi—Left Gate Guard General and director of palace eunuch affairs—was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 力士承恩歳久，中外畏之。

translations.literal: Lishi had enjoyed imperial favor for many years, and both inside and outside the court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi had enjoyed the emperor's favor for many years, and the whole court, inside and out, feared him.

sentences.zh: 太子亦呼之爲兄，諸王公呼之爲翁，駙馬輩直謂之爺，自李林甫、安祿山輩皆因之以取將相。

translations.literal: The crown prince also called him Elder Brother; the various princes called him Sir; the imperial sons-in-law simply called him Grandfather. From Li Linfu and An Lushan onward, all relied on him to obtain posts as generals and chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince called him Elder Brother; the princes called him Sir; the imperial sons-in-law called him Grandfather. From Li Linfu and An Lushan on, everyone who sought a general's or minister's post went through him.

sentences.zh: 其家富厚不貲。

translations.literal: His household was wealthy beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: His household was fabulously wealthy.

sentences.zh: -{於}-西京作寶壽寺，寺-{鐘}-成，力士作齋以慶之，舉朝畢集。

translations.literal: In the Western Capital he built Baoshou Temple; when the temple bell was completed, Lishi held a vegetarian feast to celebrate it, and the whole court assembled.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an he built Baoshou Temple. When the temple bell was cast, Lishi held a feast to dedicate it, and the entire court turned out.

sentences.zh: 撃-{鐘}-一杵，施錢百緡，，有求媚者至二十杵，少者不減十杵。

translations.literal: For each stroke on the bell one gave a hundred strings of cash; those seeking favor gave as many as twenty strokes, and none gave fewer than ten.
translations.idiomatic: Each stroke of the bell cost a hundred strings of cash. Flatterers gave as many as twenty strokes; no one gave fewer than ten.

sentences.zh: 然性和謹少過，善觀時俯仰，不敢驕橫，故天子終親任之，士大夫亦不疾惡也。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was mild and cautious with few faults; he was skilled at reading the times and bending or straightening accordingly, and did not dare act arrogantly. Therefore the Son of Heaven to the end trusted him personally, and the scholar-officials did not greatly detest him either.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was by nature cautious and seldom erred. He read the times well and never dared grow arrogant. The emperor therefore continued to trust him, and even the scholar-officials did not wholly despise him.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬午，群臣上尊號曰開元天寶聖文神武應道皇帝；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day renwu, the ministers presented a honorific title: Emperor of Kaiyuan, Tianbao, Sagely Culture, Divine Martial, and Responsive to the Way;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day renwu, the ministers offered the honorific title Emperor of Kaiyuan, Tianbao, Sagely Culture, Divine Martial, and Responsive to the Way;

sentences.zh: 赦天下，免百姓來載租庸，擇-{後}-魏子孫一人爲三恪。

translations.literal: an amnesty was proclaimed for the realm, the people's land and corvée taxes for the coming year were remitted, and one descendant of the Later Wei was chosen as one of the Three Venerable Lines.
translations.idiomatic: a general amnesty was declared, land and corvée taxes for the coming year were remitted, and one descendant of the Later Wei was named among the Three Venerable Lines.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚子，賜安祿山鐵券。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day gengzi, An Lushan was granted an iron certificate of immunity.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day gengzi, An Lushan was granted an iron certificate of immunity.

sentences.zh: 度支郎中兼侍-{御}-史楊釗善窺上意所愛惡而迎之，以聚斂驟遷，歳中領十五-{餘}-使。

translations.literal: Yang Zhao, director in the Revenue Bureau and concurrently attendant censor, was skilled at discerning what the emperor loved or hated and catering to it; through revenue extraction he was rapidly promoted, and within the year held more than fifteen commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao of the Revenue Bureau, who also served as attendant censor, was adept at reading the emperor's moods and pandering to them. Through ruthless revenue extraction he rose rapidly, and within a year held more than fifteen commissions.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，遷給事中，兼-{御}-史中丞，專判度支事，恩幸日隆。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen he was transferred to supervising secretary, concurrently vice censor-in-chief, with sole charge of revenue affairs; his favor and trust grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiachen he was made supervising secretary and vice censor-in-chief, with sole charge of revenue affairs. Imperial favor toward him grew daily.

sentences.zh: 蘇冕論曰：設官分職，各有司存。

translations.literal: Su Mian commented: When offices are established and duties divided, each has its proper charge.
translations.idiomatic: Su Mian wrote: When offices are established and duties divided, each has its proper charge.

sentences.zh: 政有恆而易守，事歸本而難失，經遠之理，-{捨}-此奚據！

translations.literal: Government has constants and is easy to maintain; affairs return to their roots and are hard to lose—for governing far into the future, on what else can one rely!
translations.idiomatic: Policy has fixed principles and is easy to uphold; affairs have their proper roots and are hard to lose. What other foundation is there for long-range governance?

sentences.zh: 洎-{奸}-臣廣言利以邀恩，多立使以示寵，刻下民以厚斂，張虚數以獻狀；

translations.literal: But when treacherous ministers widely spoke of profit to win favor, multiplied commissions to display favoritism, carved the common people to enrich exactions, and inflated false figures to present reports;
translations.idiomatic: But when corrupt ministers preached profit to win favor, multiplied special commissions to display patronage, squeezed the people for heavier levies, and inflated figures in their reports;

sentences.zh: 上心蕩而益奢，人望怨而成禍；

translations.literal: the ruler's heart grew unsteady and ever more extravagant, popular expectation turned to resentment and became disaster;
translations.idiomatic: the emperor's mind grew restless and ever more extravagant, public resentment turned to disaster;

sentences.zh: 使天子有司守其位而無其事，愛厚祿而虚其用。

translations.literal: and the Son of Heaven's regular officials kept their posts but had no real duties, cherishing generous salaries while their offices stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: and the regular officials kept their titles but had no real work, drawing generous salaries for empty posts.

sentences.zh: 宇文融首唱其端，楊愼矜、王□繼遵其軌，楊國忠終成其亂。

translations.literal: Yuwen Rong first raised this tune; Yang Shenjin and Wang [Hong] followed in his track; Yang Guozhong in the end brought the disorder to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Rong started this pattern; Yang Shenjin and Wang Hong followed it; Yang Guozhong brought the ruin to completion.

sentences.zh: 仲尼-{云}-：「-{寧}-有盜臣，而無聚斂之臣。」

translations.literal: Confucius said, "Better to have thieving ministers than revenue-extracting ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Better to have thieving ministers than revenue-extracting ministers."

sentences.zh: 誠哉是言！

translations.literal: How true those words are!
translations.idiomatic: How true those words are!

sentences.zh: 前車既覆，-{後}-轍未改，求達化本，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: The cart ahead has already overturned, yet the tracks behind are unchanged—how hard it is to seek the root of far-reaching transformation!
translations.idiomatic: The warning cart has already overturned, yet the tracks behind remain unchanged. How can one hope to reach the root of lasting reform?

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚戌，上幸華淸宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day gengxu, the emperor visited Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day gengxu, the emperor visited Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸未，以貴妃姊-{適}-崔氏者爲韓國夫人，-{適}-裴氏者爲虢國夫人，-{適}-柳氏者爲秦國夫人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day guiwei, the imperial consort's elder sister married to the Cui clan was made Lady of Han, she married to the Pei clan was made Lady of Guo, and she married to the Liu clan was made Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day guiwei, the imperial consort's elder sisters—the one married to the Cui clan, the one married to the Pei clan, and the one married to the Liu clan—were ennobled as Ladies of Han, Guo, and Qin respectively.

sentences.zh: 三人皆有-{才}-色，上呼之爲姨，出入宮掖，-{並}-承恩澤，勢傾天下。

translations.literal: All three had talent and beauty; the emperor called them Aunt, they came and went within the palace women's quarters, all alike received his grace, and their power tilted the realm.
translations.idiomatic: All three were talented and beautiful. The emperor called them Aunt. They moved freely within the inner palace, shared his favor equally, and their power overshadowed the realm.

sentences.zh: 毎命婦入見，玉眞公主等皆讓不敢就位。

translations.literal: Whenever titled ladies were summoned to audience, Princess Yuzhen and the others yielded and dared not take their seats.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court ladies were summoned to audience, Princess Yuzhen and the others stepped aside and dared not take their seats.

sentences.zh: 三姊與銛、錡五家，凡有請-{托}-，府縣承迎，峻-{於}--{制}-敕；

translations.literal: The three sisters together with the families of Xian and Qi—five households in all—whenever they made requests, prefectures and counties received them with greater urgency than imperial edicts;
translations.idiomatic: The three sisters and the families of Xian and Qi—five households in all—were obeyed by every prefecture and county with more urgency than an imperial edict whenever they made a request;

sentences.zh: 四方賂遺，輻湊其門，惟恐居-{後}-，朝夕如市。

translations.literal: bribes and gifts from the four directions converged on their gates; all feared to come last, and morning and evening their doors were like a market.
translations.idiomatic: gifts and bribes poured in from every quarter. Supplicants feared to arrive last; their gates were as busy as a market from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 十宅諸王及百孫院婚嫁，皆先以錢千緡賂韓、虢使請，無不如-{志}-。

translations.literal: When the princes of the Ten Residences and the Hundred-Grandsons Institute sought marriages, all first gave a thousand strings of cash in bribes to the Ladies of Han and Guo to make the request, and none failed to obtain their wish.
translations.idiomatic: When princes of the Ten Residences or the Hundred-Grandsons Institute sought a marriage, they first paid a thousand strings of cash to the Ladies of Han and Guo to intercede—and none failed to get what they wanted.

sentences.zh: 上所賜與及四方獻遺，五家如一。

translations.literal: What the emperor bestowed and what the four directions presented as gifts were divided equally among the five households.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the emperor bestowed or the provinces sent as tribute was divided equally among the five households.

sentences.zh: 競開第-{捨}-，極其壯麗，一堂之費，運逾千萬；

translations.literal: They vied to build mansions of the utmost splendor; the cost of a single hall often exceeded ten million;
translations.idiomatic: They vied to build mansions of spectacular grandeur. A single hall often cost more than ten million cash;

sentences.zh: 既成，見它人有勝己者，輒毀而改爲。

translations.literal: once finished, if they saw another's surpass theirs, they would tear it down and rebuild.
translations.idiomatic: and once finished, if they saw someone else's surpass theirs, they tore it down and rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 虢國尤爲豪蕩，一旦，帥工徒突入韋嗣立宅，即撤去舊屋，自爲新第，但授韋氏以隙地十畝而已。

translations.literal: The Lady of Guo was especially extravagant and unrestrained. One day she led workmen in a sudden entry into Wei Sili's residence, immediately tore down the old buildings, and built a new mansion for herself, giving the Wei clan only ten mu of leftover land.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Guo was the most extravagant of all. One day she marched workmen into Wei Sili's house, demolished it, and built a new mansion for herself, leaving the Wei family only ten mu of vacant land.

sentences.zh: 中堂既成，召工圬墁，約錢二百萬；

translations.literal: When the central hall was completed, she summoned plasterers and agreed on a fee of two million cash;
translations.idiomatic: When the central hall was finished, she summoned plasterers and agreed on a fee of two million cash;

sentences.zh: -{復}-求賞技，虢國以絳羅五百段賞之，嗤而不顧，曰：「請取螻蟻、蜥蜴，記其數置堂中，苟失一物，不敢受直。」

translations.literal: he then asked to be rewarded for his skill. The Lady of Guo gave him five hundred bolts of crimson silk; he sneered and paid no heed, saying, "Please count the ants and lizards, record their numbers, and place them in the hall. If a single one is missing, I dare not accept payment."
translations.idiomatic: then asked for a bonus for his skill. The Lady of Guo offered five hundred bolts of crimson silk. He scoffed and refused, saying, "Count every ant and lizard in the hall and mark their numbers. If even one is missing when I finish, I will not take your money."

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊戌，或言玄元皇帝降-{於}-朝元閣，-{制}-改會昌縣曰昭應，廢新-{豐}-入昭應。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day wuxu, someone reported that the Emperor of Profound Origin had descended at Chaoyuan Pavilion; by edict Huichang County was renamed Zhaoying, and Xinfeng was abolished and annexed to Zhaoying.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day wuxu, someone reported that the Emperor of Profound Origin had descended at Chaoyuan Pavilion. By edict Huichang County was renamed Zhaoying, and Xinfeng was abolished and merged into it.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上還宮。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰-{築}-神威軍-{於}-靑海上，吐蕃至，翰撃破之。

translations.literal: Geshu Han built the Shenwei Army on the Qinghai frontier; when the Tibetans arrived, Han defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han established the Shenwei Army on the Qinghai frontier. When Tibetans attacked, he routed them.

sentences.zh: 又-{築}-城-{於}-靑海中龍駒島，謂之應龍城，吐蕃屛跡不敢近靑海。

translations.literal: He also built a fortress on Longju Island in Qinghai, called it Yinglong City, and the Tibetans withdrew and dared not approach Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: He also built a fortress on Longju Island in Qinghai called Yinglong City. The Tibetans withdrew and dared not approach the region again.

sentences.zh: 是歳，-{雲}-南王歸義卒，子閣羅鳳嗣，以其子鳳迦異爲陽瓜州刺史。

translations.literal: This year the King of Yunnan, Piluoge, died; his son Geluofeng succeeded him and appointed his son Fengjiayi prefect of Yanggua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year King Piluoge of Yunnan died. His son Geluofeng succeeded him and appointed his son Fengjiayi prefect of Yanggua.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，戊申，引百官觀左藏，賜帛有差。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on the day wushen, he led the hundred officials to view the Left Treasury and bestowed silks in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, on the day wushen, the emperor led the officials to view the Left Treasury and bestowed silk gifts in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 是時州縣殷富，倉庫積粟帛，動以萬計。

translations.literal: At this time prefectures and counties were prosperous; storehouses piled grain and silk in amounts reckoned by the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties were prosperous then; storehouses held grain and silk in amounts reckoned by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 楊釗奏請所在糶變爲輕貨，及-{-{征}-}-丁租地稅皆變布帛輸京師；

translations.literal: Yang Zhao memorialized asking that everywhere grain be sold and converted to light goods, and that corvée, land, and other taxes all be converted to cloth and silk for delivery to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao proposed that local grain reserves be sold for portable goods and that corvée, land, and other taxes be collected in cloth and silk for shipment to the capital;

sentences.zh: 屢奏帑藏充牣，古今罕儔，故上帥群臣觀之，賜釗紫衣金魚以賞之。

translations.literal: he repeatedly reported that the treasury stores were full to overflowing, rarely matched in past or present; therefore the emperor led the ministers to view them and rewarded Zhao with purple robes and a golden fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: he repeatedly reported that the treasury was fuller than at any time in memory. The emperor therefore led the court to inspect it and rewarded Zhao with purple robes and a golden fish tally.

sentences.zh: 上以國用-{豐}-衍，故視金帛如糞壤，賞賜貴寵之家，無有限極。

translations.literal: Because state revenues were abundant, the emperor regarded gold and silk like dung and soil, and bestowed gifts on favored noble houses without limit.
translations.idiomatic: With state revenues overflowing, the emperor treated gold and silk like dirt, showering favored households with gifts without limit.

sentences.zh: 三月，朔方節度等使張齊丘-{於}-中受降城西北五百-{餘}--{里}-木刺山-{築}-橫塞軍，以振遠軍使鄭人郭子儀爲橫塞軍使。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhang Qiqiu, military commissioner of Shuofang and other posts, built the Hengsai Army at Muci Mountain five hundred-odd li northwest of Zhongshoujiang City, and appointed Guo Ziyi of Zheng, commander of the Zhenyuan Army, as commander of the Hengsai Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhang Qiqiu, commissioner of Shuofang and other circuits, established the Hengsai Army at Muci Mountain, five hundred-odd li northwest of Zhongshoujiang City, and appointed Guo Ziyi of Zheng, commander of the Zhenyuan Army, to lead it.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，-{咸}--{寧}-太守趙奉璋告李林甫罪二十-{餘}-條；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Zhao Fengzhang, prefect of Xianning, accused Li Linfu of more than twenty crimes;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Zhao Fengzhang, prefect of Xianning, submitted a petition accusing Li Linfu of more than twenty crimes;

sentences.zh: 狀未達，林甫知之，諷-{御}-史逮捕，以爲妖言，杖殺之。

translations.literal: the petition had not yet arrived when Linfu learned of it, prompted the censors to arrest him, treated it as demonic speech, and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: before the petition reached the capital Linfu learned of it, had the censors arrest Zhao, denounced the charges as seditious rumor, and had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 先是，折-{衝}-府皆有木契、銅魚，朝廷-{-{征}-}--{發}-，下敕書、契、魚，都督、郡府參驗皆合，然-{後}-遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, every zhechong garrison had wooden tallies and bronze fish; when the court mobilized troops it issued edicts, tallies, and fish, and only after the regional commander and prefectural offices verified that all matched were troops dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Previously every zhechong garrison held wooden tallies and bronze fish tokens. When the court mobilized troops it issued edicts, tallies, and tokens together; only after regional and prefectural offices verified that all matched were troops dispatched.

sentences.zh: 自募置擴騎，府兵日益墮壞，死及逃亡者，有司不-{復}-點補；

translations.literal: Since the recruitment of the expanded cavalry, the militia grew daily more ruined; those who died or fled were no longer checked and replaced by the authorities;
translations.idiomatic: After the expanded cavalry was recruited, the militia system decayed steadily. Deaths and desertions went unreplaced;

sentences.zh: 其六馱馬牛、器械、糗糧，耗散略盡。

translations.literal: their transport animals, equipment, and rations were largely exhausted and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: their pack animals, weapons, and rations were largely exhausted.

sentences.zh: 府兵入宿衞者，謂之侍官，言其爲天子侍衞也。

translations.literal: Militiamen who entered palace guard service were called attendant officers, meaning that they attended and guarded the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Militiamen assigned to palace guard duty were called attendant officers—men who stood guard for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 其-{後}-本衞多以假人，役使如奴隸，長安人羞之，至以相詬病。

translations.literal: Afterward the original guards mostly used hired substitutes, treating them like slaves; people of Chang'an were ashamed of this and even used it as a term of abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Later the guards mostly hired substitutes and treated them like slaves. Chang'an society was ashamed of this—it became a term of abuse.

sentences.zh: 其戍邊者，又多爲邊將苦使，利其死而沒其財。

translations.literal: Those garrisoned on the frontier were often harshly worked by frontier generals, who profited from their deaths and seized their property.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrison troops were often worked to death by their commanders, who seized their property when they died.

sentences.zh: 由是應爲府兵者皆逃匿，至是無兵可交。

translations.literal: Because of this all who should have served as militia fled and hid themselves; by this time there were no troops left to hand over.
translations.idiomatic: Men liable for militia service fled and hid. By now there were no troops left to deliver.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸酉，李林甫奏停折-{衝}-府上下魚書；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day guiyou, Li Linfu memorialized to abolish the exchange of fish tallies between upper and lower zhechong garrisons;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day guiyou, Li Linfu memorialized to abolish the exchange of fish tallies between zhechong garrisons;

sentences.zh: 是-{後}-府兵徒有官吏而已。

translations.literal: after this the militia existed in name only as officials.
translations.idiomatic: after which the militia existed only as empty offices.

sentences.zh: 其折-{衝}-、果毅，又歴年不遷，士大夫亦恥爲之。

translations.literal: The zhechong and guoyi officers, moreover, went years without promotion, and scholar-officials were ashamed to hold such posts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhechong and guoyi officers went years without promotion, and the gentry were ashamed to hold such posts.

sentences.zh: 其擴騎之法，天寶以-{後}-，稍亦變廢，應募者皆市井負販、無賴子弟，未嘗習兵。

translations.literal: The expanded-cavalry system, after the Tianbao era, also gradually fell into disuse; those who enlisted were all market peddlers and worthless young men who had never practiced arms.
translations.idiomatic: The expanded-cavalry system too fell into decay after the Tianbao era. Recruits were market peddlers and idle young men who had never trained as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 時承平日久，議者多謂中國兵可銷，-{於}-是民間挾兵器者有禁；

translations.literal: Peace had lasted long; many in discussion said the armies of China could be abolished, and therefore the people were forbidden to carry weapons;
translations.idiomatic: After long peace many argued that China's armies could be abolished, and civilians were forbidden to carry weapons;

sentences.zh: 子弟爲武官，父兄擯不齒。

translations.literal: when sons and younger brothers became military officers, fathers and elder brothers rejected them and would not rank them as equals.
translations.idiomatic: and when a son took a military post, his family disowned him.

sentences.zh: 猛將精兵，皆聚-{於}-西北邊，中國無武備矣。

translations.literal: Fierce generals and elite troops were all massed on the northwestern frontier; the heartland had no military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's best generals and troops were massed on the northwestern frontier. The heartland had no military strength left.

sentences.zh: 太白山人李渾等上言見神人，言金星洞有玉板石記聖主福壽之符；

translations.literal: Li Hun of Taibai Mountain and others reported that they had seen a divine being, who said that in Golden Star Cave there was a jade plaque recording the sage ruler's talisman of fortune and long life;
translations.idiomatic: Li Hun of Taibai Mountain and others reported seeing a divine being who said that Golden Star Cave held a jade plaque inscribed with a talisman of fortune and long life for the sage emperor;

sentences.zh: 命-{御}-史中丞王□入仙-{遊}--{谷}-求而獲之。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang [Yue] to enter Immortal Roaming Valley to seek it, and he obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Yue to search Immortal Roaming Valley, and the plaque was found.

sentences.zh: 上以符瑞相繼，皆祖宗休烈，六月，戊申，上聖祖號曰大道玄元皇帝，上髙祖謚曰神堯大聖皇帝，大宗謚曰文武大聖皇帝，髙宗謚曰天皇大聖皇帝，中宗謚曰孝和大聖皇帝，睿宗謚曰玄眞大聖皇帝，竇太-{后}-以下皆加謚曰順聖皇-{后}-。

translations.literal: Because omens and auspicious signs followed one another, all the glorious achievements of the ancestors, in the sixth month, on the day wushen, he elevated the Sagely Ancestor's title to Emperor of the Great Way and Profound Origin, raised Gaozu's posthumous title to Divine Yao Great Sage Emperor, Taizong's to Civil and Martial Great Sage Emperor, Gaozong's to Heavenly Sovereign Great Sage Emperor, Zhongzong's to Filial and Harmonious Great Sage Emperor, Ruizong's to Profound Truth Great Sage Emperor, and from Empress Dowager Dou downward all received the added posthumous title of Complaisant Sage Empress.
translations.idiomatic: With auspicious omens appearing in succession—the blessings of his ancestors—in the sixth month, on the day wushen, he elevated the Sagely Ancestor to Emperor of the Great Way and Profound Origin, raised the posthumous titles of Gaozu, Taizong, Gaozong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong to Great Sage Emperor, and from Empress Dowager Dou downward added the posthumous title Complaisant Sage Empress to the imperial consorts.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，刑部尚書、京兆尹蕭炅坐贓左遷汝陰太守。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, Xiao Jiong, Minister of Justice and metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, was demoted for corruption to prefect of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinhai, Xiao Jiong, Minister of Justice and metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, was demoted to prefect of Ruyin on charges of corruption.

sentences.zh: 上命隴右節度使哥舒翰帥隴右、河西及突厥阿布思兵，益以朔方、河東兵，凡六萬三千，攻吐蕃石堡城。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Geshu Han, military commissioner of Longyou, to lead the Longyou, Hexi, and Türk Abusi forces, reinforced with Shuofang and Hedong troops, altogether sixty-three thousand, to attack the Tibetan fortress of Shibao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Geshu Han, military commissioner of Longyou, to lead Longyou, Hexi, and Türk Abusi forces, reinforced with troops from Shuofang and Hedong—altogether sixty-three thousand men—to attack the Tibetan fortress of Shibao.

sentences.zh: 其城三-{面}-險絶，惟一徑可上，吐蕃但以數百人守之，多貯糧食，積檑木及石，唐兵前-{後}-屢攻之，不能克。

translations.literal: The city was precipitous and impassable on three sides; only one path led up. Tibetans stationed only a few hundred men to guard it, storing much grain and piling beams and stones. Tang troops attacked repeatedly from front and rear but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The fortress was sheer on three sides, with only a single path to the summit. The Tibetans held it with just a few hundred men, stockpiled grain, and heaped rolling logs and stones. Tang forces assaulted it again and again from every direction but could not break through.

sentences.zh: 翰進攻數日不拔，召裨將髙秀巖、張守瑜，欲斬之，二人請三日期可克；

translations.literal: Han pressed the attack for several days without success, summoned subordinate generals Gao Xiuyan and Zhang Shouyu intending to execute them; the two asked for three days, saying they could capture it.
translations.idiomatic: After days of failed assaults, Han summoned his subordinate generals Gao Xiuyan and Zhang Shouyu to behead them. They begged three days' grace, promising the city would fall within that time.

sentences.zh: 如期拔之，獲吐蕃鐵刃悉諾羅等四百人，唐士卒死者數萬，果如王忠嗣之言。

translations.literal: On schedule they took it, capturing four hundred Tibetans including Tieren Sinuoluo; Tang soldiers who died numbered in the tens of thousands—exactly as Wang Zhongsi had said.
translations.idiomatic: They took the city on time, capturing four hundred Tibetans including Tieren Sinuoluo. Tang dead ran into the tens of thousands—just as Wang Zhongsi had warned.

sentences.zh: 頃之，翰又遣兵-{於}-赤嶺西開屯田，以謫卒二千戍龍駒島；

translations.literal: Before long Han again sent troops west of Chiling to open military colonies and stationed two thousand exiled convicts to garrison Longju Island.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Han sent troops west of Chiling to open military farms and posted two thousand banished convicts to garrison Longju Island.

sentences.zh: 冬冰合，吐蕃大集，戍者盡沒。

translations.literal: When winter ice closed in, Tibetans massed in force and the garrison was entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: When winter froze the waters, the Tibetans gathered in strength and wiped out the entire garrison.

sentences.zh: 閏月，乙-{丑}-，以石堡城爲神武軍，又-{於}-劍南西山索磨川置保-{寧}-都護府。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day yichou, Shibao city was made the Shenwu Army, and the Baoning Protectorate was established at Suomo River in the western mountains of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on yichou, Shibao was designated the Shenwu Army, and the Baoning Protectorate was set up on the Suomo River in the western mountains of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，上謁太淸宮。

translations.literal: On bingyin the emperor visited the Taiqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the emperor paid homage at the Taiqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，群臣上尊號曰開元天地大寶聖文神武應道皇帝，赦天下。

translations.literal: On dingmao the officials presented the honorific title Emperor of Kaiyuan, Heaven and Earth, Great Treasure, Sagely Culture, Divine Military, and Responsive Way, and amnestied the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the court presented the title Emperor of Kaiyuan, Heaven and Earth, Great Treasure, Sagely Culture, Divine Military, and Responsive Way, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 禘、祫自今-{於}-太淸宮聖祖前設位序正。

translations.literal: From now on the di and xia sacrifices would have their tablet order set correctly before the Sacred Ancestor in the Taiqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the di and xia rites would have their ritual placements ordered correctly before the Sacred Ancestor in the Taiqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，冊突騎施移撥爲十姓可汗。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Yibo of the Turgesh was enfeoffed as Khaghan of the Ten Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Yibo of the Turgesh was invested as Khaghan of the Ten Surnames.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙亥，護蜜王羅眞檀入朝，請留宿衞；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yihai, King Luozhentan of Humi came to court and asked to remain in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yihai, King Luozhentan of Humi arrived at court and asked to stay on as an imperial guardsman.

sentences.zh: 許之，拜左武衞將軍。

translations.literal: The request was granted; he was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted, and he was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙-{丑}-，上幸華淸宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yichou, the emperor visited Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yichou, the emperor went to Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙未，吐火羅-{葉}-護失裡怛伽羅遣使表稱：「朅師王親附吐蕃，因苦小勃律鎭軍，阻其糧道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yiwei, the Protector of Tuhuoluo, Shilitanjialuo, sent envoys with a memorial stating: "The king of Kucha has attached himself to Tibet and harasses the garrison of Lesser Bolü, blocking their supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yiwei, Shilitanjialuo, protector of Tuhuoluo, sent envoys with a memorial: "The king of Kucha has sided with Tibet and is harrying the Lesser Bolü garrison, cutting off their grain routes.

sentences.zh: 臣思破兇徒，望-{發}-安西兵，以來歳正月至小勃律，六月至大勃律。」

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to break these villains and asks that Anxi troops be dispatched to reach Lesser Bolü by the first month of the coming year and Greater Bolü by the sixth month."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to destroy these enemies and ask that Anxi forces march so as to reach Lesser Bolü by the first month of next year and Greater Bolü by the sixth."

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted the request.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥，上還宮。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jihai, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jihai, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 群臣屢表請封西-{嶽}-，許之。

translations.literal: The officials repeatedly memorialized requesting investiture of the Western Marchmount; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers repeatedly petitioned for a feng sacrifice at the Western Marchmount, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 二月，楊貴妃-{復}-忤旨，送歸私第。

translations.literal: In the second month, Yang Guifei again offended the emperor's intent and was sent back to her private residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Imperial Consort Yang again displeased the emperor and was sent home to her family mansion.

sentences.zh: 戸部郎中吉温因宦官言-{於}-上曰：「婦人識慮不遠，違忤聖心，陛下何愛宮中一席之地，不使之就死，豈忍辱之-{於}-外-{捨}-邪？」

translations.literal: Ji Wen, Director in the Ministry of Revenue, had an eunuch speak to the emperor, saying: "A woman's judgment does not reach far. Having violated the sacred heart, why should Your Majesty cherish a single place in the palace and not have her put to death? Can you bear to have her humiliated in an outer dwelling?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen, a director in the Ministry of Revenue, had an eunuch tell the emperor: "Women's foresight is short. She has offended your sacred will—why cherish one corner of the palace and not let her die? Why endure the shame of keeping her in an outer house?"

sentences.zh: 上亦悔之，遣中使賜以-{御}-膳。

translations.literal: The emperor also regretted it and sent a palace envoy to bestow imperial fare.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted it too and sent a palace envoy with imperial provisions.

sentences.zh: 妃對使者涕泣曰：「妾罪當死，陛下幸不殺而歸之。

translations.literal: The consort wept to the envoy and said: "Your servant's crime deserves death; His Majesty was merciful not to kill me but sent me home.
translations.idiomatic: The consort wept before the envoy and said: "My crime deserves death. His Majesty was merciful not to execute me but sent me away.

sentences.zh: 今當永離掖庭，金玉珍玩，皆陛下所賜，不足爲獻，惟-{發}-者父母所與，敢以-{薦}-誠。」

translations.literal: Now I must forever leave the inner court. Gold, jade, and curios—all gifts from His Majesty—are not fit to offer; only my hair, given by my parents, do I dare present in sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Now I must leave the inner palace forever. Gold, jade, and treasures—all your gifts—are unworthy to offer back; only my hair, which my parents gave me, do I dare present as proof of my devotion."

sentences.zh: 乃剪-{髮}-一繚而獻之。

translations.literal: She then cut off a lock of hair and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: She then cut off a lock of hair and sent it as an offering.

sentences.zh: 上遽使髙力士召還，寵待益深。

translations.literal: The emperor hastily sent Gao Lishi to summon her back; favor grew deeper still.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once sent Gao Lishi to bring her back, and his favor for her deepened further.

sentences.zh: 時諸貴戚競以進食相尚，上命宦官姚思藝爲檢校進食使，水陸珍羞數千盤，一盤費中人十家之産。

translations.literal: At the time the great clans vied in offering food; the emperor appointed the eunuch Yao Siyi superintendent of presented foods. Delicacies from land and water numbered thousands of platters; one platter cost the livelihood of ten middle-class households.
translations.idiomatic: The great clans were then competing to send delicacies, and the emperor named the eunuch Yao Siyi commissioner to inspect such offerings. Land and sea delicacies ran to thousands of dishes; a single dish could cost what ten middling households lived on.

sentences.zh: 中書-{舍}-人竇華嘗退朝，値公主進食，列-{於}-中衢，傳呼按轡出其間，宮苑小兒數百奮梃-{於}-前，華僅以身免。

translations.literal: Dou Hua, Secretariat drafter, was leaving court when he encountered a princess's food procession lined along the central avenue. Criers ordered riders to rein in and pass through. Several hundred palace lads brandished clubs before them; Hua barely escaped bodily harm.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Hua, a drafting secretary, was leaving court when he met a princess's food train lined along the main thoroughfare. Heralds shouted for riders to rein in and thread through. Several hundred palace boys swung clubs before him; Hua barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 安西節度使髙仙芝破朅師，虜其王勃特沒。

translations.literal: Gao Xianzhi, military commissioner of Anxi, defeated Kucha and captured its king Botemo.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianzhi, military commissioner of Anxi, crushed Kucha and took its king Botemo captive.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚子，立勃特沒之兄素迦爲朅師王。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengzi, Botemo's elder brother Sujia was installed as king of Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengzi, Botemo's elder brother Sujia was enthroned as king of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 上命-{御}-史大夫王□鑿華山路，設壇塲-{於}-其上。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Censor-in-Chief Wang Si to cut a road on Mount Hua and set an altar platform atop it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Censor-in-Chief Wang Si to hew a path on Mount Hua and erect a ritual platform on the summit.

sentences.zh: 是春，關中旱，辛亥，-{岳}-祠災；

translations.literal: That spring there was drought in Guanzhong; on xinhai the marchmount shrine burned.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Guanzhong suffered drought, and on xinhai the marchmount shrine caught fire.

translations.literal: An edict canceled the Western Marchmount investiture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict canceled the planned feng at the Western Marchmount.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己巳，-{御}-史中丞宋渾坐贓巨萬，流潮陽。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jisi, Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Hun was convicted of bribes in the tens of thousands and exiled to Chaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jisi, Vice Censor-in-Chief Song Hun was found guilty of bribes worth tens of thousands and was exiled to Chaoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，吉温因李林甫得進；

translations.literal: Earlier Ji Wen had advanced through Li Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ji Wen had risen through Li Linfu's patronage.

sentences.zh: 及兵部侍郎兼-{御}-史中丞楊釗恩遇浸深，温遂去林甫而附之，爲釗畫代林甫執政之策。

translations.literal: When Yang Zhao's favor deepened as Vice Minister of War and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, Wen left Linfu to attach to him and plotted how Zhao could replace Linfu in power.
translations.idiomatic: As Yang Zhao, Vice Minister of War and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, grew ever more favored, Wen abandoned Linfu for Zhao and devised a plan for Zhao to supplant Linfu at the helm.

sentences.zh: 蕭炅及渾，皆林甫所厚也，求得其罪，使釗奏而逐之，以剪其心腹，林甫不能救也。

translations.literal: Xiao Jiong and Hun were both men Linfu favored; Wen found their crimes and had Zhao memorialize to expel them, pruning Linfu's inner circle—Linfu could not save them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jiong and Hun were both protégés of Linfu. Wen uncovered their crimes and had Zhao memorialize for their removal, cutting away Linfu's trusted men—Linfu could not protect them.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙卯，賜安祿山爵東平郡王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yimao, An Lushan was granted the title Prince of Dongping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yimao, An Lushan was created Prince of Dongping commandery.

sentences.zh: 唐將帥封王自此始。

translations.literal: This was the beginning of Tang generals receiving princely titles.
translations.idiomatic: From this point Tang military commanders began to receive princely enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙亥，置廣文館-{於}-國子監，以教諸生習進士者。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on yihai, the Guangwen Hall was established in the Directorate of Education to instruct students preparing for the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on yihai, the Guangwen Hall was set up within the Directorate of Education to train students for the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁巳，以安祿山兼河北道採訪處置使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dingsi, An Lushan was also made Investigating and Disposing Commissioner of the Hebei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingsi, An Lushan was additionally appointed Investigating and Disposing Commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度使張齊丘給糧失宜，軍士怒，毆其判官；

translations.literal: Zhang Qiqiu, military commissioner of Shuofang, distributed rations improperly; the soldiers were angry and beat his aide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiqiu, military commissioner of Shuofang, issued rations badly; the troops were furious and beat his aide.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使郭子儀以身捍齊丘，乃得免。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, army marshal, shielded Qiqiu with his body and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, army marshal, threw himself in the way to shield Qiqiu, and Qiqiu escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，齊丘左遷濟陰太守，以河西節度使安思順權知朔方節度事。

translations.literal: On guihai Qiqiu was demoted to prefect of Jiyin; An Sishun, military commissioner of Hexi, was appointed provisional commander of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Zhang Qiqiu was demoted to prefect of Jiyin, and An Sishun, military commissioner of Hexi, was named acting commander of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，處士崔昌上言：「國家宜承周、漢，以土代火；

translations.literal: On xinmao the recluse Cui Chang submitted: "The state should follow Zhou and Han, using Earth to supplant Fire;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the recluse Cui Chang memorialized: "The dynasty should follow Zhou and Han, taking Earth to succeed Fire;

sentences.zh: 周、隋皆閏位，不當以其子孫爲二王-{后}-。」

translations.literal: Zhou and Sui were both irregular successions and their descendants should not serve as the two dynasties honored after the imperial house."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Sui were usurping lines and their descendants ought not stand as the two collateral houses honored after the throne."

sentences.zh: 事下公卿集議。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to collective deliberation by the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent down for deliberation by the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 集賢院學士衞包上言：「集議之夜，四星聚-{於}-尾，天意昭然。」

translations.literal: Wei Bao, academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, submitted: "On the night of the assembly, four stars gathered in the Tail constellation—the intent of Heaven is manifest."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bao, an academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, wrote: "On the night of the conference, four stars gathered in the Tail—Heaven's will is plain."

sentences.zh: 上乃命求殷、周、漢-{後}-爲三恪，廢韓、介、巂公；

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered that descendants of Yin, Zhou, and Han be sought as the Sanke, abolishing the Dukes of Han, Jie, and Juan;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered descendants of Yin, Zhou, and Han sought as the Sanke, and abolished the lines of Han, Jie, and Juan;

sentences.zh: 以昌爲左贊善大夫，包爲虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: Chang was made Left Mentor, Bao made Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chang was appointed Left Mentor, and Wei Bao Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚申，上幸華淸宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, the emperor visited Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on gengshen, the emperor went to Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 太白山人王玄翼上言見玄元皇帝，言寶仙洞有妙寶眞符。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanyi, a man of Mount Taibai, reported seeing the Mysterious Prime Emperor and said the Precious Immortal Grotto held wondrous true talismans.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanyi, a recluse of Mount Taibai, claimed he had seen the Mysterious Prime Emperor and that the Precious Immortal Grotto held miraculous true talismans.

sentences.zh: 命刑部尚書張均等往求，得之。

translations.literal: He ordered Minister of Justice Zhang Jun and others to seek them; they obtained them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Minister of Justice Zhang Jun and others to fetch them, and they succeeded.

sentences.zh: 時上尊道教，慕長生，故所在爭言符瑞，群臣表賀無虚月。

translations.literal: The emperor now honored Daoism and longed for immortality, so everywhere people competed to report portents; ministers' congratulatory memorials left no month empty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now exalted Daoism and yearned for long life, so the empire vied to report omens, and congratulatory memorials from the court scarcely missed a month.

sentences.zh: 李林甫等皆請-{舍}-宅爲觀以祝聖壽，上悅。

translations.literal: Li Linfu and others all asked to yield their mansions for temples to pray for the sage's longevity; the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu and the rest all asked to turn their mansions into temples to pray for the sage's long life, and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 安祿山屢誘奚、契丹，爲設會，飲以莨菪酒，醉而坑之，動數千人，函其酋長之首以獻，前-{後}-數四。

translations.literal: An Lushan repeatedly lured the Xi and Khitan to feasts, gave them henbane wine, and when drunk buried them alive—often several thousand at a time—packing chieftains' heads to present; this happened three or four times in succession.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan repeatedly enticed Xi and Khitan leaders to banquets, plied them with henbane wine, and when they were drunk buried them alive—often several thousand at once—then sent the chieftains' heads in boxes as tribute; he did this three or four times running.

sentences.zh: 至是請入朝，上命有司先爲起第-{於}-昭應。

translations.literal: At this time he requested to come to court; the emperor ordered the authorities first to build him a mansion in Zhaoying.
translations.idiomatic: Now he asked to attend court, and the emperor ordered officials to build him a residence at Zhaoying beforehand.

sentences.zh: 祿山至戲水，楊釗兄弟姊妹皆往迎之，冠蓋蔽野；

translations.literal: When Lushan reached Xishui, Yang Zhao's brothers and sisters all went to meet him; caps and canopies covered the fields.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan reached Xishui, Yang Zhao's brothers and sisters all rode out to greet him; parasols and carriage canopies blanketed the countryside.

sentences.zh: 上自幸望春宮以待之。

translations.literal: The emperor himself visited Wangchun Palace to await him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself went to Wangchun Palace to wait for him.

sentences.zh: 辛未，祿山獻奚俘八千人，上命考課之日書上上考。

translations.literal: On xinwei Lushan presented eight thousand Xi captives; the emperor ordered that on the day of performance review he be recorded highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Lushan presented eight thousand Xi captives, and the emperor ordered that his annual evaluation be marked the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 前此-{聽}-祿山-{於}-上-{谷}-鑄錢五壚，祿山乃獻錢樣千緡。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had permitted Lushan to cast coin at five furnaces in Shanggu; Lushan now presented one thousand strings of sample coin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had allowed Lushan five mint furnaces at Shanggu; now Lushan presented a thousand strings of sample coinage.

sentences.zh: 楊釗，張易之之甥也，奏乞昭雪易之兄弟。

translations.literal: Yang Zhao was a nephew of Zhang Yizhi; he memorialized asking to clear the names of Yizhi and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao was Zhang Yizhi's nephew and memorialized asking to rehabilitate Yizhi and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，-{制}-引易之兄弟迎中宗-{於}-房陵之功，-{復}-其官爵，仍賜一子官。

translations.literal: On gengchen an edict cited the merit of Yizhi's brothers in welcoming Zhongzong from Fangling, restored their offices and titles, and granted an office to one son each.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen an edict recalled how Yizhi's brothers had helped bring Zhongzong back from Fangling, restored their ranks and titles, and granted an office to one son of each.

sentences.zh: 釗以圖讖有「金刀」，請更名；

translations.literal: Zhao, because prognostic texts contained "gold knife," requested a name change.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, because prophecy books contained the phrase "gold knife" (the character Liu dissected), asked to change his name.

sentences.zh: 上賜名國忠。

translations.literal: The emperor granted the name Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed the name Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙亥，上還宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yihai, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yihai, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 關西-{遊}-弈使王難得撃吐蕃，克五橋，拔樹敦城，以難得爲白水軍使。

translations.literal: Wang Nande, recreational commissioner of Guanxi, attacked Tibet, took five bridges, captured Shudun city, and Nande was made commander of the Baishui Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Nande, Guanxi recreational commissioner, struck the Tibetans, seized five bridges, took Shudun city, and was appointed commander of the Baishui Army.

sentences.zh: 安西四鎭節度使髙仙芝偽與石國約和，引兵襲之，虜其王及部衆以歸，悉殺其老弱。

translations.literal: Gao Xianzhi, military commissioner of the four Anxi garrisons, feigned peace with the Stone Kingdom, led troops in a surprise attack, captured its king and people, and killed all the old and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianzhi, commissioner of the four Anxi garrisons, pretended to make peace with the Stone Kingdom, then struck by surprise, carried off its king and populace, and slaughtered every aged and weak person.

sentences.zh: 仙芝性貪，掠得瑟瑟十-{餘}-斛，黃金五六橐駝，其-{餘}-口馬雜貨稱是，皆入其家。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was greedy by nature; he plundered more than ten hu of lapis lazuli, five or six camel-loads of gold, and other livestock and goods in like measure—all went into his household.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was rapacious by nature: he seized more than ten hu of lapis lazuli, five or six camels' loads of gold, and comparable stocks of people, horses, and goods—all of it went into his private store.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠德鮮-{于}-仲通，-{薦}-爲劍南節度使。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong was indebted to Xian Yu Zhongtong and recommended him as military commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong owed Xian Yu Zhongtong a debt of gratitude and had him appointed military commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 仲通性褊急，失蠻夷心。

translations.literal: Zhongtong was narrow and impatient by nature and lost the hearts of the southwestern tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongtong was narrow and hot-tempered by nature and alienated the southwestern tribes.

sentences.zh: 故事，南詔常與妻子倶謁都督，過-{雲}-南，-{雲}-南太守張虔陀皆私之。

translations.literal: By precedent Nanzhao would visit the regional commander with his wife; passing through Yunnan, Prefect Zhang Qiantuo would molest them.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the king of Nanzhao would visit the regional commander with his wife; when they passed through Yunnan, Prefect Zhang Qiantuo would take liberties with her.

sentences.zh: 又多所-{-{徴}-}-求，南詔王閣羅鳳不應，虔陀遣人詈辱之，仍密奏其罪。

translations.literal: He also demanded much; King Geluofeng of Nanzhao refused. Qiantuo sent men to revile and insult him and secretly memorialized his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He also levied excessive demands. King Geluofeng of Nanzhao refused, so Qiantuo sent men to curse and humiliate him while secretly memorializing charges against him.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳忿怨，是歳，-{發}-兵反，攻陷-{雲}-南，殺虔陀，取夷州三十二。

translations.literal: Geluofeng was resentful; that year he raised troops in rebellion, took Yunnan, killed Qiantuo, and seized thirty-two Yi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng burned with resentment; that year he raised an army in revolt, overran Yunnan, killed Qiantuo, and took thirty-two Yi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬辰，上朝獻太淸宮；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renchen the emperor offered at the Taiqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renchen the emperor made offerings at the Taiqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，朝享太廟；

translations.literal: On guisi he worshipped at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he performed rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 甲子，合祀天地-{於}-南郊，赦天下，免天下今載地稅。

translations.literal: On jiazi he performed the combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb, amnestied the realm, and exempted land tax for the current year throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he offered the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the Southern Suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, and remitted the land tax for that year empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，命李林甫遙領朔方節度使，以戸部侍郎李□知留-{後}-事。

translations.literal: On dingyou Li Linfu was appointed distant-command military commissioner of Shuofang, and Vice Minister of Revenue Li Hui was made acting rear commander.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Li Linfu was named titular military commissioner of Shuofang, while Vice Minister of Revenue Li Hui was left in charge as acting rear commander.

sentences.zh: 庚子，楊氏五宅夜-{遊}-，與廣平公主從者爭西市門，楊氏奴揮鞭及公主衣，公主墜馬，駙馬程昌裔下扶之，亦被數鞭。

translations.literal: On gengzi the five Yang mansions went out at night and contended with the Princess of Guangping's attendants at the west market gate; a Yang slave swung a whip that struck the princess's garment; she fell from her horse; her consort Cheng Changyi dismounted to support her and was also struck several times.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the five Yang households were out at night and quarreled with the Princess of Guangping's escort at the west market gate. A Yang bondsman lashed out with his whip and caught the princess's robe; she was thrown from her horse. Her consort Cheng Changyi leapt down to help her and was whipped several times as well.

sentences.zh: 公主泣訴-{於}-上，上爲之杖殺楊氏奴。

translations.literal: The princess tearfully complained to the emperor, who had the Yang slave beaten to death for her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess wept before the emperor, and he had the Yang bondsman beaten to death on her account.

sentences.zh: 明日，免昌裔官，不-{聽}-朝謁。

translations.literal: The next day Changyi was removed from office and forbidden court audience.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Cheng Changyi was stripped of office and barred from court attendance.

sentences.zh: 上命有司爲安祿山起第-{於}-親仁坊，敕令但窮壯麗，不限財力。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the authorities to build a mansion for An Lushan in Qinren Ward, decreeing that it should be magnificent without limit on expense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered officials to raise a mansion for An Lushan in Qinren Ward, instructing them to make it as grand as possible with no ceiling on cost.

sentences.zh: 既成，具幄帟器皿，充牣其中，有貼白檀床二，皆長丈，闊六尺；

translations.literal: When completed, curtains, hangings, and vessels filled it; there were two white-sandalwood beds with gold inlay, each a zhang long and six chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished, hangings and vessels packed every room. There were two white-sandalwood beds inlaid with gold, each a zhang long and six chi wide.

sentences.zh: 銀平脱屛風，帳一方一丈八尺；

translations.literal: Silver pingtuo screens; a canopy eighteen chi square.
translations.idiomatic: There were silver pingtuo screens and a canopy eighteen chi on a side.

sentences.zh: -{於}-廚廄之物皆飾以金銀，金飯罌二，銀淘盆二，皆受五-{斗}-，織銀絲筐及笊籬各一；

translations.literal: Kitchen and stable goods were all gilt with gold and silver—two golden rice jars and two silver washing basins, each holding five dou; one woven silver basket and one strainer each.
translations.idiomatic: Even kitchen and stable fittings were trimmed in gold and silver: two gold rice pots and two silver rinsing basins, each holding five dou, plus one silver-woven basket and one strainer.

sentences.zh: 他物稱是。

translations.literal: Other things were in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else matched in scale.

sentences.zh: 雖禁中服-{御}-之物，殆不及也。

translations.literal: Even items for imperial use in the palace scarcely matched.
translations.idiomatic: Even furnishings reserved for the inner palace scarcely compared.

sentences.zh: 上毎令中使爲祿山護役，-{築}-第及儲偫賜物，常戒之曰：「胡眼大，勿令笑我。」

translations.literal: The emperor often had eunuchs oversee Lushan's labor, building the mansion and storing gifts, and would warn them: "Barbarian eyes are wide—do not let him laugh at me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor constantly sent eunuchs to supervise Lushan's building and the stockpiling of gifts, warning them: "The barbarian's eyes are large—do not let him laugh at my stinginess."

sentences.zh: 祿山入新第，置酒，乞降墨敕請宰相至第。

translations.literal: Lushan entered his new mansion, set out wine, and begged an autograph edict inviting the chief ministers to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan moved into his new mansion, held a feast, and asked for an autograph edict summoning the chief ministers to his house.

sentences.zh: 是日，上欲-{於}-樓下撃球，遽爲罷戲，命宰相赴之。

translations.literal: That day the emperor was about to play ball below the tower; he abruptly canceled the game and ordered the ministers to attend.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor had meant to play cuju beneath the tower; he broke off the game at once and sent the ministers to Lushan's feast.

sentences.zh: 日遣諸楊與之選勝-{游}-宴，侑以梨園教坊樂。

translations.literal: Daily he sent the various Yangs to join him at scenic outings and feasts, accompanied by Pear Garden and Music Bureau performers.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he dispatched the Yang clan to join Lushan on pleasure outings and banquets, with Pear Garden and Music Bureau artists to entertain them.

sentences.zh: 上毎食一物稍美，或-{後}-苑校獵獲鮮禽，輒遣中使走馬賜之，絡驛-{於}-路。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor ate something especially fine, or when the rear park hunt brought fresh game, he would dispatch eunuchs at a gallop to bestow them—messengers relaying along the road without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor tasted something especially fine, or when a hunt in the rear park yielded fresh game, he would send eunuchs galloping to Lushan with gifts—couriers riding in relays without pause.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，祿山生日，上及貴妃賜衣服、寶器、酒饌甚厚。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Lushan's birthday, the emperor and the imperial consort bestowed clothes, treasures, food, and drink in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Lushan's birthday, the emperor and Imperial Consort Yang lavished on him robes, treasures, food, and wine.

sentences.zh: -{後}-三日，召祿山入禁中，貴妃以錦繡爲大襁褓，裹祿山，使宮人以彩輿舁之。

translations.literal: Three days later Lushan was summoned into the inner palace; the consort wrapped him in a great brocade swaddling-cloth and had palace women carry him in a colored litter.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Lushan was called into the inner palace. The consort bound him in a great brocade swaddling-cloth and had palace women lift him in a painted litter.

sentences.zh: 上聞-{後}-宮喧笑，問其故，左右以貴妃三日洗祿兒對。

translations.literal: Hearing uproarious laughter from the rear palace, the emperor asked the reason; attendants answered that the consort was performing the three-day "bath the Lushu child" ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing loud laughter from the rear palace, the emperor asked why; attendants said the consort was holding the three-day ceremony to "bathe the child Lushan."

sentences.zh: 上自往觀之，喜，賜貴妃洗兒金銀錢，-{復}-厚賜祿山，盡歡而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor went in person to watch, was pleased, bestowed gold and silver money for bathing the child on the consort, richly rewarded Lushan again, and the revel ended in full joy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to look on, was delighted, gave the consort gold and silver for the bathing gift, heaped further rewards on Lushan, and the party broke up in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 自是祿山出入宮掖不禁，或與貴妃對食，或通宵不出，頗有-{丑}-聲聞-{於}-外，上亦不疑也。

translations.literal: From then on Lushan came and went within the palace without restriction; sometimes he dined facing the consort, sometimes stayed out all night—ugly rumors spread outside, but the emperor was not suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: After that Lushan entered and left the palace precincts unchecked—sometimes dining face to face with the consort, sometimes not emerging all night. Ugly talk circulated outside, yet the emperor suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 安西節度使髙仙芝入朝，獻所擒突騎施可汗、吐蕃酋長、石國王、朅師王。

translations.literal: Gao Xianzhi, military commissioner of Anxi, came to court and presented captives: the Turgesh khaghan, Tibetan chieftains, the king of the Stone Kingdom, and the king of Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianzhi, military commissioner of Anxi, arrived at court and presented prisoners: the Turgesh khaghan, Tibetan chiefs, the king of the Stone Kingdom, and the king of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 加仙芝開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was promoted to Grand Mentor with the Palace Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was advanced to Grand Mentor of the Palace Corps with honorary credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 尋以仙芝爲河西節度使，代安思順；

translations.literal: Soon thereafter Xianzhi was made military commissioner of Hexi, replacing An Sishun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xianzhi was appointed military commissioner of Hexi in place of An Sishun.

sentences.zh: 思順諷群胡割耳剺-{面}-請留己，-{制}--{復}-留思順-{於}-河西。

translations.literal: An Sishun induced the various Hu to cut their ears and scar their faces to request that he himself be kept; an edict again kept An Sishun in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: An Sishun stirred the Hu followers to mutilate themselves—cutting ears and slashing faces—to beg that he be retained in command; the throne then ordered him kept in Hexi after all.

sentences.zh: 安祿山求兼河東節度。

translations.literal: An Lushan requested to hold concurrently the Hedong military commission.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan asked to take the Hedong command in addition to his existing posts.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙辰，以河東節度使韓休鈱爲左羽林將軍，以祿山代之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingchen, Han Xiujian, military commissioner of Hedong, was made Left Director of the Forest of Feathers, and Lushan replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day bingchen, Hedong commissioner Han Xiujian was transferred to the Left Forest of Feathers, and Lushan took his place.

sentences.zh: 戸部郎中吉温見祿山有寵，又附之，約爲兄弟，説祿山曰：「李右丞相雖以時事親三兄，必不肯以兄爲相；

translations.literal: Ji Wen, bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, saw that Lushan had favor and attached himself to him; they contracted brotherhood. He said to Lushan: "Right Chancellor Li, though he may for the moment treat Third Brother affectionately, will certainly not make Brother chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen of the Revenue Bureau saw Lushan riding high in favor and clung to him; they swore brotherhood. Wen told Lushan, "Chancellor Li may play the fond uncle for now, but he will never put you in the chief ministership;

sentences.zh: 温雖蒙驅使，終不得超擢。

translations.literal: Though Wen may be employed on errands, in the end he will not win rapid promotion.
translations.idiomatic: I may run his errands, yet I will never rise past the middle ranks.

sentences.zh: 兄若-{薦}-温-{於}-上，温即奏兄堪大任，共排林甫出之，爲相必矣。」

translations.literal: If Brother recommends Wen to His Majesty, Wen will memorialize that Brother is fit for great responsibility; together we drive Linfu out and make him chancellor—this is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Recommend me to the throne, and I will testify that you are the man for the top post—we will push Linfu aside together, and the chancellorship is yours."

sentences.zh: 祿山悅其言，數稱温-{才}--{於}-上，上亦忘曩日之言。

translations.literal: Lushan was pleased with his words and repeatedly praised Wen's talent to the emperor; the emperor also forgot his words of former days.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan liked the scheme and praised Wen's ability again and again before the emperor, who had by now forgotten what he had once said against him.

sentences.zh: 會祿山領河東，因奏温爲節度副使、知留-{後}-，以大理司直張通儒爲留-{後}-判官，河東事悉以委之。

translations.literal: When Lushan came to hold Hedong, he memorialized that Wen be made vice military commissioner and acting regent, with Zhang Tongru, chief of the Court of Judicial Review, as registrar under the regent—all Hedong affairs were entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lushan took Hedong, he had Wen appointed deputy commissioner and acting regent, with Zhang Tongru of the Court of Judicial Review as the regent's registrar; the whole circuit was placed in their hands.

sentences.zh: 是時，楊國忠爲-{御}-史中丞，方承恩用事。

translations.literal: At this time Yang Guozhong was vice censor-in-chief and was just receiving favor and wielding power.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong was then vice censor-in-chief, newly swollen with imperial favor and office.

sentences.zh: 祿山登降殿階，國忠常扶掖之。

translations.literal: When Lushan ascended and descended the hall steps, Guozhong would often steady him.
translations.idiomatic: On the palace steps Lushan would climb and descend, and Guozhong would steady him by the arm.

sentences.zh: 祿山與王□倶爲大夫，□權任亞-{於}-李林甫。

translations.literal: Lushan and Wang Hong were both grand councillors; Hong's power ranked second only to Li Linfu's.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan and Wang Hong both held the grand councillor's rank; Hong's authority stood only beneath Li Linfu's.

sentences.zh: 祿山見林甫，禮貌頗倨。

translations.literal: When Lushan saw Linfu, his demeanor was quite arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: In Linfu's presence Lushan carried himself with open arrogance.

sentences.zh: 林甫陽以他事召王大夫，□至，趨拜甚謹，祿山不覺自失，容貌益恭。

translations.literal: Linfu, under the pretext of other business, summoned Grand Councillor Wang; when Hong arrived, he hurried to bow with great deference. Lushan, without realizing it, felt himself at a loss and grew more respectful in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu, on a pretext of other business, called in Councillor Wang. Hong came at once and bowed with painstaking deference. Lushan, watching, felt his own assurance slip away and straightened his manner still further.

sentences.zh: 林甫與祿山語，毎揣知其情，先言之，祿山驚服。

translations.literal: Whenever Linfu spoke with Lushan, he would each time divine Lushan's mind and state it first; Lushan was startled into admiration.
translations.idiomatic: In every conversation Linfu seemed to read Lushan's thoughts and speak them first; Lushan was shaken into admiration.

sentences.zh: 祿山-{於}-公卿皆慢侮之，獨憚林甫，毎見，雖盛冬，常汗沾衣。

translations.literal: Toward the high ministers Lushan was all contemptuous and insulting, yet he alone feared Linfu; whenever he met him, even in deep winter sweat would soak his robes.
translations.idiomatic: He treated the court nobles with contempt, yet he alone feared Linfu; even in the depth of winter he would meet him drenched in sweat.

sentences.zh: 林甫乃引與坐-{於}-中書廳，撫以温言，自解披袍以覆之。

translations.literal: Linfu then led him to sit in the Central Secretariat hall, soothed him with gentle words, and himself removed his outer robe to cover him.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu drew him into the Secretariat hall, spoke to him kindly, and took off his own outer robe to lay over Lushan's shoulders.

sentences.zh: 祿山忻荷，言無不盡，謂林甫爲十郎。

translations.literal: Lushan was delighted and obliged, spoke without reserve, and called Linfu "Tenth Son."
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was grateful and unguarded, telling him everything, and called him "Young Master Ten."

sentences.zh: 既歸-{范}-陽，劉駱-{谷}-毎自長安來，必問：「十郎何言？」
