translations.literal: After returning to Fanyang, whenever Liu Luogu came from Chang'an he would always ask: "What does Tenth Son say?"
translations.idiomatic: Back in Fanyang, whenever Liu Luogu arrived from the capital he would ask at once, "What did Young Master Ten say?"

sentences.zh: 得美言則喜；

translations.literal: If he heard pleasant words he was pleased;
translations.idiomatic: Good news made him glad;

sentences.zh: 或但-{云}-「語安大夫，須好檢校！」

translations.literal: Or if he only said, "Tell the An councillor he must guard himself carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: but if the message was only, "Tell Councillor An to watch himself!"

sentences.zh: 輒反手據床曰：「噫嘻，我死矣！」

translations.literal: He would turn, slap the bed, and cry, "Alas—I am done for!"
translations.idiomatic: He would wheel about, strike the couch, and wail, "Then I am finished!"

sentences.zh: 祿山既兼領三鎭，賞刑己出，日益驕恣。

translations.literal: Lushan had now come to hold three circuits concurrently; rewards and punishments issued from his own hand, and he grew daily more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan now commanded three frontier circuits at once; reward and punishment flowed from his own desk, and his pride swelled by the day.

sentences.zh: 自以曩時不拜太子，見上春秋髙，頗内懼；

translations.literal: He remembered that in former times he had not bowed to the heir apparent, and seeing that the emperor's years were high, he was quite fearful within;
translations.idiomatic: He recalled that he had once refused to bow to the crown prince, and with the emperor's age mounting, fear gnawed at him;

sentences.zh: 又見武備墮馳，有輕中國之心。

translations.literal: He also saw that martial preparations had fallen into decay, and within him he came to hold the Middle Kingdom lightly.
translations.idiomatic: he also saw arms and discipline rotting in the interior, and began to think lightly of the empire itself.

sentences.zh: 孔目官嚴莊、掌書記髙尚因爲之解圖讖，勸之作亂。

translations.literal: Kongmu officer Yan Zhuang and chief secretary Gao Shang therefore explained prognostic charts for him and urged rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His staff officers Yan Zhuang and Gao Shang read the omens for him and pressed him toward revolt.

sentences.zh: 祿山養同羅、奚、契丹降者八千-{餘}-人，謂之「曳落河」。

translations.literal: Lushan supported more than eight thousand surrendered men of the Toghuz, Xi, and Khitan whom he called "yeluohe."
translations.idiomatic: He kept more than eight thousand Toghuz, Xi, and Khitan who had surrendered to him, calling them the yeluohe.

sentences.zh: 曳落河者，胡言壯士也。

translations.literal: Yeluohe means "brave warriors" in the Hu tongue.
translations.idiomatic: In the northern languages yeluohe means "brave men."

sentences.zh: 及家僮百-{餘}-人，皆驍勇善戰，一可當百。

translations.literal: With more than a hundred household slaves, all fierce and skilled in war—each could match a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred household retainers, all hardened fighters, were said to match a hundred ordinary soldiers each.

sentences.zh: 又畜戰馬數萬匹，多聚兵仗，分遣商胡詣諸道販鬻，歳輸珍貨數百萬。

translations.literal: He also kept tens of thousands of war horses and amassed many weapons, sending merchant Hu to various circuits to trade; each year he forwarded rare goods worth millions.
translations.idiomatic: He stockpiled tens of thousands of warhorses and mountains of weapons, sent Sogdian traders along every route, and every year poured millions in treasure toward his camps.

sentences.zh: 私作緋紫袍、魚袋、以百萬計。

translations.literal: Privately he made crimson and purple robes and fish purses by the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In secret his workshops turned out court robes and official insignia by the hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 以髙尚、嚴莊、張通儒及將軍孫孝哲爲腹心，史思明、安守忠、李歸仁、蔡希德、牛廷玠、向潤容、李庭望、崔-{乾}-祐、尹子奇、何千年、武令珣、能元皓、田承嗣、田-{乾}-眞、阿史那承慶爲爪牙。

translations.literal: He took Gao Shang, Yan Zhuang, Zhang Tongru, and the general Sun Xiaozhe as his inner circle; Shi Siming, An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, Cai Xide, Niu Tingjie, Xiang Runrong, Li Tingwang, Cui Qianyou, Yin Ziqi, He Qiannian, Wu Lingxun, Neng Yuanhao, Tian Chengsi, Tian Qianzhen, Ashina Chengqing as his claws.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shang, Yan Zhuang, Zhang Tongru, and the general Sun Xiaozhe formed his inner council; Shi Siming, An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, Cai Xide, Niu Tingjie, Xiang Runrong, Li Tingwang, Cui Qianyou, Yin Ziqi, He Qiannian, Wu Lingxun, Neng Yuanhao, Tian Chengsi, Tian Qianzhen, and Ashina Chengqing were the claws he set on the land.

sentences.zh: 尚，雍權人，本名不危，頗有辭學，薄-{游}-河朔，貧困不得-{志}-，常歎曰：「髙不危當舉大事而死，豈能嚙草根求活邪！」

translations.literal: Shang was a man of Yongquan, original name Buwei; he had considerable literary learning. Wandering in Hebei in hardship, unable to fulfill his ambition, he would often sigh: "Gao Buwei should undertake a great affair and die—how could I gnaw grass roots to stay alive?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shang came from Yongquan; his birth name was Buwei, and he was a man of real learning. Penniless on the roads of Hebei, he would sigh, "A man called Gao Buwei ought to die in a great cause—what honor is there in chewing roots to linger on?"

sentences.zh: 祿山引置幕府，出入臥内。

translations.literal: Lushan took him into his staff and admitted him to his sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan drew him into his staff and let him in and out of his private quarters.

sentences.zh: 尚典牋奏，莊治簿書。

translations.literal: Shang handled memorial drafts; Zhuang managed ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: Shang drafted the papers; Zhuang kept the accounts.

sentences.zh: 通儒，萬歳之子；

translations.literal: Tongru was the son of Wan Sui;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tongru was the son of Zhang Wansui;

sentences.zh: 孝哲，契丹出。

translations.literal: Xiaozhe was of Khitan birth.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiaozhe was born among the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 承嗣世爲盧龍小校，祿山以爲前鋒兵馬使，治軍嚴整。

translations.literal: Chengsi for generations had been a petty officer of Lulong; Lushan made him vanguard army commander and his regulations were strict.
translations.idiomatic: The Tian family had served for generations as petty officers in Lulong; Lushan made Tian Chengsi vanguard commander, and his camp ran on iron discipline.

sentences.zh: 嘗大雪，祿山按行諸營，至承嗣營，寂若無人，入閲士卒，無一人不在者，祿山以是重之。

translations.literal: Once in heavy snow Lushan inspected the camps; when he reached Chengsi's camp it was silent as if no one were there. Entering to review the troops, not a single man was absent; Lushan therefore valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Once, in a driving snow, Lushan toured the camps. Chengsi's lines were so quiet they seemed empty; yet when he entered to muster the men, every soldier was in place. From that day Lushan trusted him above the rest.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬午，劍南節度使鮮-{于}-仲通討南詔蠻，大敗-{於}-瀘南。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, renwu, Xian Yu Zhongtong, military commissioner of Jiannan, attacked the Nanzhao barbarians and was utterly defeated south of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day renwu, Jiannan commissioner Xian Yu Zhongtong marched against Nanzhao and was shattered south of Lu.

sentences.zh: 時仲通將兵八萬，分二道出戎、巂州，至-{曲}-州、靖州。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongtong was leading eighty thousand troops in two columns out of Rong and Xi prefectures to Qu and Jing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongtong had eighty thousand men in two wings, marching from Rong and Xi toward Qu and Jing.

sentences.zh: 南詔王閣羅鳳遣使謝罪，請還所俘掠，城-{雲}-南而去，且曰：「今吐蕃大兵壓境，若不許我，我將歸命吐蕃，-{雲}-南非唐有也。」

translations.literal: Nanzhao King Piluoge sent envoys to apologize, asking to return captives and plunder and abandon Yunnan and depart, saying: "Now Tibetan great armies press the border; if you do not grant my request, I shall cast my fate with Tibet—Yunnan will no longer belong to Tang."
translations.idiomatic: King Piluoge of Nanzhao sent envoys to sue for peace, offering to return prisoners and booty and withdraw from Yunnan, and warning: "Tibetan armies are already on my border. Deny me, and I throw my lot with Tibet—Yunnan will not be Tang's again."

sentences.zh: 仲通不許，囚其使。

translations.literal: Zhongtong did not consent and imprisoned the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongtong refused and clapped the envoys in chains.

sentences.zh: 進軍至西洱河，與閣羅鳳戰，軍大敗，士卒死者六萬人，仲通僅以身免。

translations.literal: Advancing to the West Er River, he fought Piluoge; the army suffered a great defeat—sixty thousand soldiers died; Zhongtong barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to the West Er River and met Piluoge in battle. Sixty thousand men died; Zhongtong alone crawled away alive.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠掩其敗狀，仍敘其戰功。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong concealed the defeat and still recounted his battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong buried the news of the rout and still entered Zhongtong's name for merit.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳斂戰屍，-{築}-爲京觀，遂北臣-{於}-吐蕃。

translations.literal: Piluoge gathered the dead from battle, piled them into a Jingguan, and then submitted north to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Piluoge heaped the Tang dead into a victory mound and then bowed north to Tibet as vassal.

sentences.zh: 蠻語謂弟爲「-{鐘}-」，吐蕃命閣羅鳳爲「贊普-{鐘}-」，號曰東帝，給以金印。

translations.literal: In the barbarian tongue "younger brother" is zhong; Tibet appointed Piluoge "Zanpu-zhong," styled Eastern Emperor, and granted him a gold seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the southern tongues "younger brother" is zhong; Tibet named him "Brother of the Zanpu," styled him Eastern Emperor, and gave him a gold seal.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳刻碑-{於}-國門，言-{於}-不得已而叛唐，且曰：「我世世事唐，受其封賞，-{後}-世容-{復}-歸唐，當指碑以示唐使者，知吾之叛非本心也。」

translations.literal: Piluoge carved a stele at the state gate saying he rebelled against Tang from necessity, and: "Our house has for generations served Tang and received enfeoffment and rewards; posterity may yet return to Tang—when that day comes, point at this stele to show Tang envoys that our rebellion was not from the heart."
translations.idiomatic: At his capital gate he set up a stone declaring that he had turned against Tang only because he must, and adding: "My line has served Tang for generations and taken its gifts. If our sons return to the empire, let them show this stone to Tang envoys and prove our hearts were never traitors."

sentences.zh: -{制}-大募兩京及河南、北兵以撃南詔；

translations.literal: An edict ordered mass conscription in the two capitals and Henan and northern forces to strike Nanzhao;
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered a great levy from the two capitals, Henan, and the northern circuits to punish Nanzhao;

sentences.zh: 人聞-{雲}-南多瘴癘，未戰士卒死者什八九，莫肯應募。

translations.literal: When people heard that Yunnan had much miasma, before battle eight or nine in ten soldiers died; none would answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: but men said Yunnan was a land of fever where eight or nine in ten died before ever seeing the enemy, and the summons went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠遣-{御}-史分道捕人，連枷送詣軍所。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong sent censors by separate routes to seize men, chaining them and delivering them to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong sent censors along every road to drag men away in chains and march them to the colors.

sentences.zh: 舊-{制}-，百姓有勳者免-{-{征}-}-役，時調兵既多，國忠奏先取髙勳。

translations.literal: By old statute, commoners with merit were exempt from corvée; as troops were levied in great numbers, Guozhong memorialized to take men of high merit first.
translations.idiomatic: By old law, men who had earned merit were excused from service; now Guozhong ordered the draft to seize the meritorious first.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是行者愁怨，父母妻子送之，所在哭聲振野。

translations.literal: Thereupon those marching were full of resentment; fathers, mothers, wives, and children escorted them—with wailing everywhere that shook the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The conscripts went off cursing; parents and wives walked beside them, and the roads shook with weeping.

sentences.zh: 髙仙芝之虜石國王也，石國王子逃詣諸胡，具告仙芝欺誘貪暴之狀。

translations.literal: When Gao Xianzhi had captured the Stone Kingdom king, the Stone Kingdom prince fled to the various Hu and fully reported Xianzhi's deception, seduction, and greedy violence.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Xianzhi seized the king of Shighnan, the prince fled to the western peoples and told them how Xianzhi had tricked, plundered, and broken faith.

sentences.zh: 諸胡皆怒，潛引大食慾共攻四鎭。

translations.literal: All the Hu were enraged and secretly invited the Arabs, wishing jointly to attack the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were furious and quietly called in the Arabs to strike the Four Garrisons together.

sentences.zh: 仙芝聞之，將蕃、漢三萬衆撃大食，深入七百-{餘}--{里}-，至恆羅斯城，與大食遇。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi heard of it, he led thirty thousand mixed Tibetan and Han troops to strike the Arabs, penetrating more than seven hundred li to Talas city, where he met the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi marched out with thirty thousand Han and allied troops, drove seven hundred li and more to Talas, and met the Arab host.

sentences.zh: 相持五日，葛羅祿部衆叛，與大食夾攻唐軍，仙芝大敗，士卒死亡略盡，所-{餘}--{才}-數千人。

translations.literal: After five days of stalemate, the Qarluq tribesmen rebelled and joined the Arabs in a pincer attack on the Tang army; Xianzhi suffered a great defeat; soldiers died almost to the last—only several thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: For five days the lines held; then the Qarluqs turned, caught the Tang between two fires, and the army was destroyed. Only a few thousand men were left alive.

sentences.zh: 右威衞將軍李嗣業勸仙芝宵遁，道路阻隘，拔汗那部衆在前，人畜塞路；

translations.literal: Right General of Majestic Guards Li Siye urged Xianzhi to flee by night; the roads were narrow and blocked—the Bukhara tribesmen were ahead, men and livestock choking the road;
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye of the Majestic Guards urged a night retreat, but the passes were jammed—Bukhara herds and wagons blocked the way ahead;

sentences.zh: 嗣業前驅，奮大梃撃之，人馬倶斃，仙芝乃得過。

translations.literal: Siye led the vanguard, swinging a great club to strike them; men and horses perished together; only then did Xianzhi get through.
translations.idiomatic: Siye took the van and smashed a path with a great iron club, killing men and beasts alike until Xianzhi could break through.

sentences.zh: 將士相失，別將汧陽段秀實聞嗣業之聲，詬曰：「避敵先奔，無勇也；

translations.literal: Officers and men became separated; Deputy General Duan Xiushi of Qianyang heard Siye's voice and cursed: "Fleeing the enemy first—no courage;
translations.idiomatic: Officers were scattered. Duan Xiushi of Qianyang heard Siye riding past and shouted, "Running before the enemy—where is your courage?

sentences.zh: 全己棄衆，不仁也。

translations.literal: Preserving yourself and abandoning the multitude—no humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Saving yourself and leaving the ranks—where is your humanity?

sentences.zh: 幸而得達，獨無愧乎！」

translations.literal: Fortunate enough to get through—are you not ashamed!"
translations.idiomatic: You escaped—and you feel no shame?"

sentences.zh: 嗣業執其手謝之，留拒追兵，收散卒，得倶免。

translations.literal: Siye grasped his hand in apology, stayed behind to hold off pursuers, gathered scattered troops, and all escaped together.
translations.idiomatic: Siye seized his hand in remorse, turned back to cover the retreat, rallied the lost, and brought them out together.

sentences.zh: 還至安西，言-{於}-仙芝，以秀實兼都知兵馬使，爲己判官。

translations.literal: Returning to Anxi, he reported to Xianzhi and had Xiushi made concurrent director of army affairs as his registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Anxi he spoke for Xiushi to Xianzhi, who made him deputy director of army affairs and his own registrar.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙辰，武庫火，燒兵器三十七萬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, bingchen, the arsenal caught fire and burned three hundred seventy thousand weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingchen, the imperial arsenal burned, destroying three hundred seventy thousand weapons.

sentences.zh: 安祿山將三道兵六萬以討契丹，以奚騎二千爲鄕導，過平盧千-{餘}--{里}-，至土護眞水，遇雨。

translations.literal: An Lushan was about to lead sixty thousand troops of three circuits against the Khitan, with two thousand Xi horsemen as guides; passing more than a thousand li through Pinglu, they reached the Tuhuluozhen River and met rain.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan took sixty thousand men from three commands against the Khitan, with two thousand Xi cavalry as guides. After a thousand li through Pinglu they came to the Tuhuluozhen River in rain.

sentences.zh: 祿山引兵晝夜兼行三百-{餘}--{里}-，至契丹牙帳，契丹大駭。

translations.literal: Lushan marched troops day and night for more than three hundred li to the Khitan royal encampment; the Khitan were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: He forced a march of three hundred li in a day and a night straight to the Khitan royal camp; the Khitan were stunned.

sentences.zh: 時久雨，弓駑筋膠皆弛，大將何思德言-{於}-祿山曰：「吾兵雖多，遠來疲弊，實不可用，不如按甲息兵以臨之，不過三日，虜必降。」

translations.literal: Long rain had slackened bowstrings and crossbow sinews; Grand General He Side said to Lushan: "Our troops though numerous, coming from afar are weary and in fact unusable—better to hold armor and rest the army facing them; within three days the barbarians will certainly surrender."
translations.idiomatic: The rains had soaked bows and crossbows useless. He Side, his chief general, said, "We are many but spent from the march—we cannot fight. Camp here and wait; in three days they will yield."

sentences.zh: 祿山怒、欲斬之，思德請前驅效死。

translations.literal: Lushan was enraged and wished to behead him; Side begged to lead the van and die in service.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan raged and would have killed him; Side begged to ride the van and die if he must.

sentences.zh: 思德貌類祿山，虜爭撃，殺之，以爲已得祿山，勇氣增倍。

translations.literal: Side's appearance resembled Lushan's; the barbarians fought to strike him and killed him, thinking they had got Lushan; their courage doubled.
translations.idiomatic: He Side looked like Lushan himself; the Khitan threw everything at him, killed him, and thought they had slain Lushan. Their spirits soared.

sentences.zh: 奚-{復}-叛，與契丹合，夾撃唐兵，殺傷殆盡。

translations.literal: The Xi rebelled again, joined the Khitan, and pincered the Tang army; killed and wounded were nearly total.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Xi turned coat, joined the Khitan, and crushed the Tang from both sides until almost no one was left standing.

sentences.zh: 射祿山，中鞍，折冠簪，失履，獨與麾下二十騎走；

translations.literal: They shot Lushan, hitting his saddle; his hat pin broke and he lost his shoes—only with some twenty mounted followers did he flee;
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck his saddle; his hat pin snapped, his shoes fell off, and he fled with barely twenty riders;

sentences.zh: 會夜，追騎解，得入師州，歸罪-{於}-左賢王哥解、河東兵馬使魚承仙而斬之。

translations.literal: Night fell and pursuit slackened; he entered Shi Prefecture, blamed the Left Wise King Gexie and Hedong army commander Yu Chengxian and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: night hid him from pursuit, and he reached Shi Prefecture, where he blamed the Left Wise King Gexie and the Hedong commander Yu Chengxian and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 平盧兵馬使史思明懼，逃入山-{谷}-近二旬，收散卒，得七百人。

translations.literal: Shi Siming, Pinglu army commander, was afraid; he fled into valleys for nearly twenty days and gathered scattered troops—seven hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming, the Pinglu army commander, fled into the hills for nearly twenty days and scraped together seven hundred survivors.

sentences.zh: 平盧守將史定方將精兵二千救祿山，契丹引去，祿山乃得免。

translations.literal: Pinglu guard commander Shi Dingfang led two thousand picked troops to rescue Lushan; the Khitan withdrew and Lushan escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dingfang of Pinglu came with two thousand elite troops; the Khitan drew off, and Lushan lived.

sentences.zh: 至平盧，麾下皆亡，不知所出。

translations.literal: Reaching Pinglu, his followers had all fled; he knew not where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Pinglu his staff had vanished, and he had no plan left.

sentences.zh: 史思明出見祿山，祿山喜，起，執其手曰：「吾得汝，-{復}-何憂！」

translations.literal: Shi Siming came out to see Lushan; Lushan was glad, rose, grasped his hand and said: "Having got you—what further worry!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming came to him. Lushan sprang up, took his hand, and said, "With you back, what is left to fear?"

sentences.zh: 思明退，謂人曰：「向使早出，已與哥解-{並}-斬矣。」

translations.literal: Siming withdrew and said to others: "Had I come out earlier, Gexie would already have been beheaded with me."
translations.idiomatic: When Siming withdrew he told others, "Had I shown myself sooner, Gexie would have died with me instead of taking the blame alone."

sentences.zh: 契丹圍師州，祿山使思明撃卻之。

translations.literal: The Khitan besieged Shi Prefecture; Lushan sent Siming to strike them back and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan besieged Shi Prefecture; Lushan sent Siming to break the siege and drive them away.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬子，上幸華淸宮。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, renzi, the emperor visited Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day renzi, Emperor Xuanzong went to Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠使鮮-{于}-仲通表請己遙領劍南；

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong had Xian Yu Zhongtong memorialize requesting to hold Jiannan at a distance;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong had Xian Yu Zhongtong ask to keep Jiannan in name while yielding the field;

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙午，以國忠領劍南節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, bingwu, Guozhong was made military commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: in the eleventh month, on bingwu, Guozhong was given the Jiannan command.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁亥，上還宮。

translations.literal: In spring, first month, dinghai, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dinghai, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚午，命有司出粟帛及庫錢數十萬緡-{於}-兩市易惡錢。

translations.literal: In the second month, gengwu, he ordered the relevant offices to issue grain, silk, and cash from the treasury—several hundred thousand strings—into the two markets to exchange for bad coin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengwu, he ordered the ministries to pour out grain, silk, and treasury cash—hundreds of thousands of strings—into the markets to buy up debased coin.

sentences.zh: 先是，江、淮多惡錢，貴戚大商往往以良錢一易惡錢五，載入長安，市井不勝其弊，故李林甫奏請禁之，官爲易取，期一月，不輸官者罪之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiang and Huai had much bad coin; great merchants and noble kin often exchanged one good coin for five bad and shipped them into Chang'an; the markets could not bear the harm, so Li Linfu memorialized to forbid it, with the government exchanging for them—within one month those who did not surrender coin would be punished.
translations.idiomatic: For years the lower Yangzi had flooded the realm with bad copper; great houses traded one good cash for five bad and carted them to Chang'an until trade staggered. Li Linfu had the state buy them in at par and gave the realm one month to comply.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是商賈囂然，不以爲便。

translations.literal: Thereupon merchants were in an uproar and did not consider it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants roared that the scheme was unworkable.

sentences.zh: 衆共遮楊國忠馬自言，國忠爲之言-{於}-上，乃更命非鉛錫所鑄及穿穴者，皆-{聽}-用之如故。

translations.literal: The multitude together blocked Guozhong's horse to petition; Guozhong spoke for them to the emperor, and a new order was issued: except coin cast from lead and tin or pierced with holes, all might be used as before.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds stopped Guozhong's horse to plead; he carried their case to the throne, and a new edict allowed all coin that was not lead, tin, or holed to circulate as before.

sentences.zh: 三月，安祿山-{發}-蕃、漢歩騎二十萬撃契丹，欲以雪去秋之恥。

translations.literal: In the third month An Lushan launched two hundred thousand Tibetan and Han infantry and cavalry against the Khitan, wishing to wipe away last autumn's shame.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Lushan marched two hundred thousand mixed steppe and Chinese horse and foot against the Khitan to wash away last autumn's disgrace.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥阿布思來降，上厚禮之，賜姓名李獻忠，累遷朔方節度副使，賜爵奉信王。

translations.literal: Earlier the Turk Abu Si had come to surrender; the emperor treated him generously, bestowed the surname and personal name Li Xianzhong, and repeatedly promoted him to vice military commissioner of Shuofang, enfeoffing him Prince of Trust-Following.
translations.idiomatic: Years before the Turk chieftain Abu Si had surrendered; the court honored him as Li Xianzhong, raised him to deputy commissioner of Shuofang, and made him Prince of Trust-Following.

sentences.zh: 獻忠有-{才}-略，不爲安祿山下，祿山恨之；

translations.literal: Xianzhong had talent and strategy and would not submit to An Lushan; Lushan hated him;
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong was able and proud and would not bow to Lushan, who hated him for it;

sentences.zh: 至是，奏請獻忠帥同羅數萬騎，與倶撃契丹。

translations.literal: At this time he memorialized that Xianzhong command tens of thousands of Toghuz horsemen to strike the Khitan together with him.
translations.idiomatic: now Lushan asked that Xianzhong lead tens of thousands of Toghuz horse to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 獻忠恐爲祿山所害，白留-{後}-張□，請奏留不行，□不許。

translations.literal: Xianzhong feared Lushan would harm him, told regent Zhang Wei, and asked that a memorial be submitted to keep him from going; Wei did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a trap, Xianzhong appealed to the acting commissioner Zhang Wei to keep him at his post; Wei refused.

sentences.zh: 獻忠乃帥所部大掠倉庫，叛歸漠北，祿山遂頓兵不進。

translations.literal: Xianzhong then led his command in great pillaging of the storehouses and rebelled back to the northern desert; Lushan thereupon halted his army and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong then looted the frontier stores, took his tribes north, and rebelled; Lushan's army never moved.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，改吏部爲文部，兵部爲武部，刑部爲憲部。

translations.literal: On yisi the Ministry of Personnel was renamed the Ministry of Letters, the Ministry of War the Ministry of Military Affairs, the Ministry of Justice the Ministry of Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the Board of Civil Office became the Board of Letters, the Board of War the Board of Military Affairs, and the Board of Punishments the Board of Statutes.

sentences.zh: 戸部侍郎兼-{御}-史大夫、京光尹王□，權寵日盛，領二十-{餘}-使。

translations.literal: Wang Hong, vice minister of revenue concurrently censor-in-chief and Jingzhao intendant—his power and favor grew daily—held more than twenty commissionerships.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, vice minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and Jingzhao intendant, grew daily in power and favor, holding more than twenty concurrent commissions.

sentences.zh: 宅旁爲使院，文案盈積，吏求署一字，累日不得前；

translations.literal: Beside his residence he set up a commissioners' compound; documents piled high; clerks seeking one signature could not reach the front for days;
translations.idiomatic: He built a bureau compound beside his mansion where papers stacked to the ceiling and clerks waited days for a single signature;

sentences.zh: 中使賜繼不絶-{於}-門，雖李林甫亦畏避之。

translations.literal: Palace envoys' gifts followed one upon another at his gate—even Li Linfu feared and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: imperial gifts streamed to his door without pause—even Li Linfu gave him wide berth.

sentences.zh: 林甫子岫爲將作監，□子淮爲衞尉少卿，倶供奉禁中。

translations.literal: Linfu's son Song was director of palace construction; Hong's son Huai was vice director of the Palace Guards—both attended within the forbidden quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu's son Song was director of palace works; Hong's son Huai was vice director of the Palace Guards; both served inside the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 淮陵侮岫，岫常下之。

translations.literal: Huai treated Song contemptuously; Song often deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai bullied Song, and Song always yielded.

sentences.zh: 然□事林甫謹，林甫雖忌其寵，不忍害也。

translations.literal: Yet Hong served Linfu carefully; though Linfu envied his favor, he could not bear to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hong still deferred to Linfu; though Linfu envied his rise, he could not bring himself to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 准嘗帥其徒過駙馬都尉王繇，繇望塵拜伏；

translations.literal: Huai once led his followers past Imperial Son-in-law Wang Yao; Yao, seeing the dust of their approach, bowed prostrate in the road;
translations.idiomatic: Huai once marched his gang past Imperial Son-in-law Wang Yao; Yao saw the dust cloud and bowed flat in the dust.

sentences.zh: 准挾彈命-{於}-繇冠，折其玉簪，以爲戲笑。

translations.literal: Huai tucked a pellet into Yao's cap order and snapped his jade hairpin as a joke.
translations.idiomatic: Huai slipped a pellet under the clasp of Yao's cap and broke his jade pin for sport.

sentences.zh: 既而繇延准置酒，繇所尚永穆公主，上之愛女也，爲準親執刀匕。

translations.literal: Later Yao hosted Huai for wine; Yao's wife was Princess Yongmu, the emperor's beloved daughter, and she personally carved and served for Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yao then gave him wine; his wife was Princess Yongmu, the emperor's favorite daughter, and she herself carved and served Huai's portions.

sentences.zh: 准去，或謂繇曰：「鼠雖挾其父勢，君乃使公主爲之具食，有如上聞，無乃非宜？」

translations.literal: After Huai left, someone said to Yao: "That rat may lean on his father's power, yet you had the princess serve his meal—if the emperor hears of it, is this not improper?"
translations.idiomatic: When Huai had gone, someone warned Yao: "That whelp rides his father's shadow, yet you let the princess wait on him at table—if word reaches the throne, will it not be unseemly?"

sentences.zh: 繇曰：「上雖怒無害，至-{於}-七郎，死生所-{繫}-，不敢不爾。」

translations.literal: Yao said: "The emperor may rage but no harm will come—as for Master Seven, my life hangs on it; I dare not do otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: Yao said: "The Son of Heaven may flare up, yet no real harm will follow—but as for Master Seven, my life is in his hand; I dare not refuse."

sentences.zh: □弟戸部郎中銲，凶險不法，召-{術}-士任海川，問：「我有王者之相否？」

translations.literal: Hong's brother, Bureau Director Xian in the Ministry of Revenue, was vicious and lawless; he summoned the technician Ren Haichuan and asked, "Do I have the countenance of a king?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong's brother Xian, a bureau director in the Revenue Ministry, was brutal and outside the law; he called in the diviner Ren Haichuan and asked, "Do I bear the marks of kingship?"

sentences.zh: 海川懼，亡匿。

translations.literal: Haichuan was afraid and fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Haichuan was terrified and went into hiding.

sentences.zh: □恐事洩，捕得，-{托}-以他事杖殺之。

translations.literal: Hong, fearing the matter would leak, had him seized and, on a trumped-up charge, beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, afraid the story would out, had him caught and clubbed to death on a false charge.

sentences.zh: 王府司馬韋會，安定公主之子，王繇之同産也，話之私庭。

translations.literal: Wei Hui, secretariat marshal of the princely mansion, was a son of Princess Ding'an and uterine brother of Wang Yao; he spoke of this in private council.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hui, secretariat marshal of the princely establishment, was a son of Princess Ding'an and Wang Yao's full brother; he spoke of these things in private.

sentences.zh: □又使長安尉賈季鄰收會-{繫}-獄，縊殺之，繇不敢言。

translations.literal: Hong again had the Chang'an marshal Jia Jilin arrest Hui and bind him in prison, strangled him; Yao dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Hong again had the Chang'an marshal Jia Jilin seize Hui and bind him in jail, then strangled him; Yao did not dare utter a word.

sentences.zh: 銲所善刑縡，與龍武萬騎謀殺龍武將軍，以其兵作亂，殺李林甫、陳希烈、楊國忠；

translations.literal: Xian's associate Xing Zai, with the Dragon Martial Ten Thousand Riders, plotted to kill the Dragon Martial commander and use his troops to rebel, killing Li Linfu, Chen Xilie, and Yang Guozhong;
translations.idiomatic: Xian's friend Xing Zai, together with the Dragon Martial Ten Thousand Riders, plotted to kill the Dragon Martial commander, raise his troops in revolt, and murder Li Linfu, Chen Xilie, and Yang Guozhong;

sentences.zh: 前期二日，有告之者。

translations.literal: two days before the set date, someone reported it.
translations.idiomatic: two days before the appointed day, someone informed on them.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙酉，上臨朝，以告狀-{面}-授□，使捕之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yiyou, at court the emperor was handed the report in person and ordered Hong to arrest them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day yiyou, the emperor held court, was given the denunciation in person, and ordered Hong to make the arrests.

sentences.zh: □意銲在縡所，先遣人召之。

translations.literal: Hong thought Xian was at Zai's place and first sent men to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong supposed Xian was at Zai's house and first sent men to call him in.

sentences.zh: 日晏，乃命賈季鄰等捕縡。

translations.literal: Only when the day was far spent did he order Jia Jilin and others to arrest Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Not until dusk did he order Jia Jilin and the rest to seize Zai.

sentences.zh: 縡居金城坊，季鄰等至門，縡帥其黨數十人持弓刀格-{鬥}-突出。

translations.literal: Zai lived in Jincheng Ward; when Jilin arrived at the gate, Zai led dozens of his faction with bows and blades, fighting to break out.
translations.idiomatic: Zai lived in Jincheng Ward; when Jilin came to the door, Zai led several dozen followers with bows and blades and fought his way out.

sentences.zh: □與楊國忠引兵繼至，縡黨曰：「勿傷大夫人。」

translations.literal: Hong and Guozhong followed with troops; Zai's men cried, "Do not harm the Grand Madam."
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Guozhong came after with soldiers; Zai's men shouted, "Do not hurt the Grand Madam!"

sentences.zh: 國忠之傔密謂國忠曰：「賊有號，不可戰也。」

translations.literal: Guozhong's attendants whispered to Guozhong: "The rebels have a signal—do not fight."
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's servants whispered to him: "The bandits have a password—you must not engage."

sentences.zh: 縡-{斗}-且走，至皇城西南隅。

translations.literal: Zai fought while fleeing to the southwest corner of the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: Zai fought as he ran to the southwest corner of the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 會髙力士引飛龍禁軍四百至，撃縡，捕其黨，皆擒之。

translations.literal: Gao Lishi arrived leading four hundred Flying Dragon guards, struck Zai, seized his followers—all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lishi came with four hundred Flying Dragon guards, struck Zai down, and seized his party; all were taken.

sentences.zh: 國忠以狀白上，曰：「□必預謀。」

translations.literal: Guozhong reported to the emperor, saying, "Hong must have been in the plot beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong reported to the throne: "Hong must have been in on it from the start."

sentences.zh: 上以□任遇深，不應同逆；

translations.literal: The emperor, because Hong's favor was deep, would not believe he shared in treason;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, who had heaped favor on Hong, would not credit him with rebellion;

sentences.zh: 李林甫亦爲之辨解。

translations.literal: Li Linfu also pleaded his case.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu spoke in his defense as well.

sentences.zh: 上乃命特原銲不問，然意欲□表請罪之；

translations.literal: The emperor then specially pardoned Xian without inquiry, yet intended that Hong would memorialize begging punishment;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then specially spared Xian further inquiry, yet expected Hong to memorialize begging punishment;

sentences.zh: 使國忠諷之，□不忍，上怒。

translations.literal: he had Guozhong hint at it; Hong could not bear to, and the emperor grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: he had Guozhong drop hints; Hong could not bring himself to do it, and the emperor's anger flared.

sentences.zh: 會陳希烈極言□大逆當誅，戊子，敕希烈與國忠鞫之，仍以國忠兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: Then Chen Xilie said forcefully that Hong's great treason deserved death; on wuzi the edict ordered Xilie and Guozhong to try him, and Guozhong was also made Jingzhao intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xilie then insisted that Hong's capital crime merited execution; on wuzi an edict put Xilie and Guozhong in charge of the trial, and Guozhong was also made Jingzhao intendant.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是任海川、韋會等事皆-{發}-，獄具，□賜自盡，銲杖死-{於}-朝堂。

translations.literal: Then the cases of Ren Haichuan, Wei Hui, and the rest were all exposed; when the dossier was complete, Hong was granted suicide and Xian was clubbed to death in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of Ren Haichuan, Wei Hui, and the rest came to light; when the file was closed, Hong was allowed to kill himself and Xian was beaten to death in the audience hall.

sentences.zh: □子准、偁流嶺南，尋殺之。

translations.literal: Hong's sons Huai and Cheng were exiled to Lingnan and soon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's sons Huai and Cheng were banished to Lingnan and soon put to death.

sentences.zh: 有司籍其第-{捨}-，數日不能遍。

translations.literal: Officials inventoried his mansions and could not finish for days.
translations.idiomatic: Officials inventoried his estates and could not complete the count for days.

sentences.zh: □賓佐莫敢窺其門，獨採訪判官裴冕收其屍葬之。

translations.literal: None of Hong's staff dared look through his gates; only the investigating registrar Pei Mian took his corpse and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: None of Hong's retainers dared approach his gates; only the investigating registrar Pei Mian gathered his body and buried it.

sentences.zh: 初，李林甫以陳希烈易-{制}-，引爲相，政事常隨林甫左右，晩節遂與林甫爲敵，林甫懼。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Linfu had brought Chen Xilie in as an easily controlled chancellor; state affairs followed Linfu's lead, but in his later years Xilie became Linfu's enemy, and Linfu grew afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Linfu had installed Chen Xilie as a pliable chancellor; government ran at Linfu's gesture, but in his last years Xilie turned enemy and Linfu was afraid.

sentences.zh: 會李獻忠叛，林甫乃請解朔方節-{制}-，且-{薦}-河西節度使安思順自代；

translations.literal: When Li Xianzhong rebelled, Linfu asked to be relieved of the Shuofang commission and recommended Hexi commissioner An Sishun to replace him;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xianzhong rebelled, Linfu asked to lay down the Shuofang command and recommended Hexi commissioner An Sishun in his place;

sentences.zh: 庚子，以思順爲朔方節度使。

translations.literal: on gengzi he made Sishun Shuofang commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: on gengzi Sishun was made Shuofang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊申，慶王琮薨，贈靖德太子。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wushen, Prince Qing Zong died; he was posthumously titled Heir Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wushen, Prince Qing Zong died and was given the posthumous title Heir Jingde.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，京兆尹楊國忠加-{御}-史大夫、京畿、關内採訪等使，凡王□所綰使務，悉歸國忠。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Jingzhao intendant Yang Guozhong was made censor-in-chief and Jijing and Guannei investigating commissioner, among others; all commissionerships Wang Hong had held passed to Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Jingzhao intendant Yang Guozhong was made censor-in-chief and Jijing and Guannei investigating commissioner, and every commission Wang Hong had held went to Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 初，李林甫以國忠微-{才}-，且貴妃之族，故善遇之。

translations.literal: Earlier Linfu had treated Guozhong well because his talent was slight and he was of the Noble Consort's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Linfu had been kind to Guozhong because his gifts were small and he belonged to the imperial consort's kin.

sentences.zh: 國忠與王□爲中丞，□用林甫-{薦}-爲大夫，故國忠不悅，遂深探刑縡獄，令引林甫交私□兄弟及阿布思事狀，陳希烈、哥舒翰從而證之；

translations.literal: Guozhong and Wang Hong had both been vice censors; Hong became grand councillor on Linfu's recommendation, so Guozhong was displeased; he dug deep into Xing Zai's case, made him implicate Linfu's private dealings with Hong's brothers and the Abu Si affair; Chen Xilie and Ge Shuhan testified as well;
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong and Wang Hong had both been vice censors; Hong had become grand councillor on Linfu's word, so Guozhong was bitter; he drove the Xing Zai investigation until it implicated Linfu's private ties with Hong's brothers and the Abu Si matter; Chen Xilie and Ge Shuhan bore witness as well;

sentences.zh: 上由是疎林甫。

translations.literal: the emperor thereby grew distant from Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor's heart turned from Linfu.

sentences.zh: 國忠貴震天下，始與林甫爲仇敵矣。

translations.literal: Guozhong's wealth and power shook the realm; he and Linfu became sworn foes.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's wealth and power shook the empire; he and Linfu were enemies at last.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲子，楊國忠奏吐蕃兵六十萬救南詔，劍南兵撃破之-{於}--{雲}-南，克敵隰州等三城，捕虜六千三百，以道遠，簡壯者千-{餘}-人及酋長降者獻之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Guozhong reported that six hundred thousand Tibetan troops had come to aid Nanzhao; Jiannan troops defeated them in Yunnan, took three cities including Diji and Yin, and captured six thousand three hundred; because the road was far, he selected a thousand-odd sturdy men and surrendering chieftains to present.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi, Guozhong reported that six hundred thousand Tibetan soldiers had marched to rescue Nanzhao; Jiannan forces routed them in Yunnan, recovered three prefectures including Diji and Yin, and took six thousand three hundred captives; the road being long, he sent on only a thousand-odd strong men and surrendering chiefs.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙-{丑}-，上-{復}-幸左藏，賜群臣帛。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on yichou, the emperor again visited the Left Treasury and bestowed silk on the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on yichou, the emperor again went to the Left Treasury and gave the ministers silk.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，楊國忠奏有鳳皇見左藏庫屋，出納判官魏仲犀言鳳集庫西通訓門。

translations.literal: On guisi, Guozhong reported that a phoenix had appeared on the roof of the Left Treasury; registrar Wei Zhongxi said phoenixes had gathered at the west Tongxun Gate of the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Guozhong reported a phoenix on the Left Treasury roof; registrar Wei Zhongxi said the birds had settled at the treasury's west Tongxun Gate.

sentences.zh: 九月，阿布思入寇，圍永淸柵，柵使張元軌拒卻之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Abu Si invaded, besieged Yongqing stockade; commandant Zhang Yuangui repulsed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Abu Si raided in, besieged Yongqing stockade, and stockade commander Zhang Yuangui drove him off.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊寅，上幸華淸宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, the emperor went to Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, the emperor visited Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 己亥，改通訓門曰鳳集門；

translations.literal: On jihai, Tongxun Gate was renamed Phoenix Gather Gate;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Tongxun Gate was renamed Phoenix Gather Gate;

sentences.zh: 魏仲犀遷殿中侍-{御}-史，楊國忠屬吏率以鳳皇優得調。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxi was promoted to palace attendant; Guozhong's subordinates mostly won favorable transfers on account of phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxi was promoted to palace attendant; Guozhong's clerks mostly gained easy promotions by trading on the phoenix.

sentences.zh: 南詔數寇邊，蜀人請楊國忠赴鎭；

translations.literal: Nanzhao raided the border repeatedly; the people of Shu asked Guozhong to go to the circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao struck the frontier again and again; men of Shu begged Guozhong to take the command;

sentences.zh: 左-{僕}-射兼右相李林甫奏遣之。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director and Right Chancellor Li Linfu memorialized to send him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director and Right Chancellor Li Linfu memorialized that he be sent.

sentences.zh: 國忠將行，泣辭上，言必爲林甫所害，貴妃亦爲之請。

translations.literal: As Guozhong was about to depart, he wept before the emperor, saying Linfu would surely harm him; the Noble Consort also pleaded for him.
translations.idiomatic: As Guozhong was leaving, he wept to the emperor that Linfu would surely destroy him; the Noble Consort pleaded too.

sentences.zh: 上謂國忠曰：「卿暫到蜀區處軍事，朕屈指待卿，還當入相。」

translations.literal: The emperor told Guozhong: "Go temporarily to Shu to manage military affairs; I count the days till your return—you will enter the chancellorship again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "Go to Shu for a time and set the armies in order; I will count the days until you return—you shall be chancellor again."

sentences.zh: 林甫時已有疾，憂懣不知所爲，巫言一見上可小愈。

translations.literal: Linfu was already ill, fretful and at a loss; sorcerers said one sight of the emperor would bring slight recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu was already sick, anxious and helpless; sorcerers said one glimpse of the emperor would ease him a little.

sentences.zh: 上欲就視之，左右固諫。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to visit him in person; attendants strongly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to go see him; those around him firmly dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 上乃命林甫出庭中，上登降聖閣遙望，以紅巾招之。

translations.literal: He had Linfu come into the courtyard; the emperor ascended the Jiangsheng Pavilion and gazed from afar, beckoning with a red scarf.
translations.idiomatic: He had Linfu come into the courtyard while he climbed the Jiangsheng Pavilion and looked from afar, waving a red scarf.

sentences.zh: 林甫不能拜，使人代拜。

translations.literal: Linfu could not bow; he had others bow for him.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu could not bow; he had someone bow in his stead.

sentences.zh: 國忠比至蜀，上遣中使召還，至昭應，謁林甫，拜-{於}-床下。

translations.literal: By the time Guozhong reached Shu, the emperor sent a palace envoy to recall him; at Zhaoying he visited Linfu and bowed at the bedside.
translations.idiomatic: Before Guozhong reached Shu, the emperor sent a palace envoy to call him back; at Zhaoying he visited Linfu and bowed at the bed.

sentences.zh: 林甫流涕謂曰：「林甫死矣，公必爲相，以-{後}-事累公！」

translations.literal: Linfu wept and said, "Linfu is dying; you will surely be chancellor—burden me with your care afterward!"
translations.idiomatic: Linfu wept and said, "Linfu is finished; you will surely be chancellor—remember me when you are!"

sentences.zh: 國忠謝不敢當，汗流覆-{面}-。

translations.literal: Guozhong declined, saying he dared not; sweat drenched his face.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong protested he dared not accept; sweat ran down his face.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁卯，林甫薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, Linfu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, Linfu died.

sentences.zh: 上晩年自恃承平，以爲天下無-{復}-可憂，遂深居禁中，專以聲色自娯，悉委政事-{於}-林甫。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor, relying on peace, thought nothing under heaven remained to worry about; he dwelled deep in the palace, indulging in music and women, entrusting all government to Linfu.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years the emperor, trusting long peace, believed the realm had no further cares; he lived deep in the palace, gave himself to pleasure, and handed all affairs to Linfu.

sentences.zh: 林甫媚事左右，迎合上意，以固其寵；

translations.literal: Linfu flattered those around the throne and met the emperor's wishes to secure his favor;
translations.idiomatic: Linfu fawned on those beside the emperor and matched his moods to keep his grace;

sentences.zh: 杜絶言路，掩蔽聰明，以成其-{奸}-；

translations.literal: he blocked all voices, veiled the emperor's clarity, to accomplish his treachery;
translations.idiomatic: he sealed off every voice and hooded the emperor's sight to finish his plots;

sentences.zh: 妬賢疾能，排抑勝己，以保其位；

translations.literal: he envied the able and hated the capable, suppressed those who surpassed him, to keep his place;
translations.idiomatic: he envied talent and feared ability, and pushed down any who outshone him to hold his seat;

sentences.zh: 屢起大獄，誅逐貴臣，以張其勢。

translations.literal: he repeatedly raised great cases, executed and banished great ministers, to expand his power.
translations.idiomatic: he opened great trials again and again, killed and exiled the high nobles, to magnify his sway.

sentences.zh: 自皇太子以下，畏之側足。

translations.literal: From the crown prince down, all feared him and walked as if on tiptoe.
translations.idiomatic: From the crown prince downward, all feared him and went in dread.

sentences.zh: 凡在相位十九年，養成天下之亂，而上不之寤也。

translations.literal: He held the chancellorship nineteen years, nurturing the empire's disorder, while the emperor never woke to it.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in the chancellorship nineteen years, nursing the empire toward chaos, while the emperor never saw it.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以楊國忠爲右相，兼文部尚書，其判使-{並}-如故。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Yang Guozhong was made Right Chancellor and concurrent Minister of Letters; his commissionerships remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Yang Guozhong was made Right Chancellor and concurrent Minister of Letters, with his other commissions unchanged.

sentences.zh: 國忠爲人強辯而輕躁，無威儀。

translations.literal: Guozhong was forceful in debate but light and rash, without dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong was sharp-tongued and volatile, without the gravity of office.

sentences.zh: 既爲相，以天下爲己任，裁決機務，果敢不疑；

translations.literal: Once chancellor, he took all under heaven as his charge, deciding urgent business boldly without doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Once in the seal he took the world as his charge, cutting through business with bold certainty;

sentences.zh: 居朝廷，攘裾扼腕，公卿以下，頤指氣使，莫不震懾。

translations.literal: in court he would hitch his robe and clutch his wrist; from the nobles down he ordered with his chin—none did not tremble.
translations.idiomatic: in the hall he would hitch his robe and clench his wrist; from the grandees down he commanded with a jerk of the chin, and none did not quake.

sentences.zh: 自侍-{御}-史至爲相，凡領四十-{餘}-使。

translations.literal: From investigating censor to chancellor he held more than forty commissionerships.
translations.idiomatic: From investigating censor to chancellor he held more than forty concurrent posts.

sentences.zh: -{台}-省官有-{才}-行時名，不爲己用者，皆出之。

translations.literal: Officials of the Secretariat and Censorate with talent and contemporary fame whom he could not use were all sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Any Secretariat or Censorate officer of talent and name whom he could not bend to his will was driven out.

sentences.zh: 或勸陝郡進士張彖謁國忠，曰：「見之，富貴立可圖。」

translations.literal: Someone urged Zhang Can, a metropolitan candidate from Shan Commandery, to call on Guozhong, saying, "See him and wealth and honor are immediately within reach."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Zhang Can, a Shan Commandery candidate, to visit Guozhong: "One audience and fortune is yours."

sentences.zh: 彖曰：「吾輩依楊右相如泰山，吾以爲冰山耳！

translations.literal: Can said, "Our sort rely on Chancellor Yang as on Mount Tai—I take him to be an iceberg!
translations.idiomatic: Can said, "We lean on Chancellor Yang as on Mount Tai—but I call him an iceberg!

sentences.zh: 若皎日既出，吾輩得無失所恃乎！」

translations.literal: When the bright sun rises, will we not lose what we lean on?"
translations.idiomatic: When the sun climbs high, will we not lose our footing?"

sentences.zh: 遂隱居-{嵩}-山。

translations.literal: He then retired to Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He went into hiding on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 國忠以司勳員外郎崔圓爲劍南留-{後}-，-{-{征}-}-魏郡太守吉温爲-{御}-史中丞，充京畿、關内採訪等使。

translations.literal: Guozhong made Vice Director of Honors Cui Yuan Jiannan regent, recalled and made Wei Commandery grand prefect Ji Wen vice censor-in-chief and Jijing and Guannei investigating commissioner, among others.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong made Vice Director of Honors Cui Yuan Jiannan regent, recalled Wei Commandery prefect Ji Wen and made him vice censor-in-chief with Jijing and Guannei investigating duties, and the like.

sentences.zh: 温詣-{范}-陽辭安祿山，祿山令其子慶緒送至境，爲温控馬出驛數十歩。

translations.literal: Wen went to Fanyang to take leave of Lushan; Lushan had his son Qingxu escort him to the border; for Wen he held the horse and walked dozens of paces from the post station.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Wen went to Fanyang to bid Lushan farewell; Lushan had his son Qingxu see him to the border and himself led Wen's horse on foot for dozens of paces beyond the relay station.

sentences.zh: 温至長安，凡朝廷動靜，輒報祿山，信宿而達。

translations.literal: When Wen reached Chang'an, every movement of the court he reported to Lushan; within two nights' post it arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Chang'an, Wen reported every shift at court to Lushan; word reached him within two post stages.

sentences.zh: 十二月，楊國忠欲收人望，建議：「文部選人，無問賢不肖，選深者留之，依資據闕注官。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Guozhong wished to win popular regard and proposed: "For civil-office candidates, regardless of worth, those of deep selection stay; offices are assigned by seniority and vacancies."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Guozhong sought popular praise and proposed: "For civil-office candidates, worthy or not, keep those of long waiting and fill posts by seniority and vacancy."

sentences.zh: 滯淹者翕然稱之。

translations.literal: Those long stalled praised it together.
translations.idiomatic: Men long blocked in office praised him together.

sentences.zh: 國忠凡所施置，皆-{曲}-徇時人所欲，故頗得衆譽。

translations.literal: In all Guozhong's measures he bent to what people of the time desired, so he gained considerable praise.
translations.idiomatic: In everything he did Guozhong bent to what men of the day wanted, and for a time he won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以平盧兵馬使史思明兼北平太守，充盧龍軍使。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Pinglu army commander Shi Siming was concurrently made Beiping grand prefect and Lulong army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Pinglu army commander Shi Siming was also made Beiping grand prefect and Lulong army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，上還宮。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以安西行軍司馬封常淸爲安西四鎭節度使。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Anxi acting army commander Feng Changqing was made Anxi Four Circuits commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Anxi acting army commander Feng Changqing was made commissioner of the four Anxi circuits.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰素與安祿山、安思順不協，上常和解之，使爲兄弟。

translations.literal: Ge Shuhan had long been at odds with An Lushan and An Sishun; the emperor often reconciled them and had them sworn as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shuhan had long been on bad terms with An Lushan and An Sishun; the emperor often patched peace between them and had them sworn as brothers.

sentences.zh: 是冬，三人倶入朝，上使髙力士宴之-{於}-城東。

translations.literal: That winter all three entered court; the emperor had Gao Lishi feast them east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: That winter all three came to court; the emperor had Gao Lishi give them a feast east of the city.

sentences.zh: 祿山謂翰曰：「我父胡，母突厥，公父突厥，母胡，族類頗同，何得不相親？」

translations.literal: Lushan said to Han, "My father was Hu, my mother Tujue; your father was Tujue, your mother Hu—our tribes are much alike; how can we not be kin?"
translations.idiomatic: Lushan said to Han, "My father was Hu and my mother Tujue; your father was Tujue and your mother Hu—we are much the same stock; how can we not be close?"

sentences.zh: 翰曰：『古人-{云}-：狐向窟嗥不祥，爲其忘本故也。

translations.literal: Han said, "The ancients said: when a fox howls toward its burrow it is ill-omened, for it forgets its roots."
translations.idiomatic: Han said, "The ancients said: when a fox howls toward its den it bodes ill, for it has forgotten its home."

sentences.zh: 兄苟見親，翰敢不盡心！」

translations.literal: "If you, brother, truly treat me as kin, how dare Han not give his whole heart!"
translations.idiomatic: "If you, brother, truly hold me kin, how dare Han not give you his whole heart!"

sentences.zh: 祿山以爲譏其胡也，大怒，罵翰曰：「突厥敢爾！」

translations.literal: Lushan took it as a barb at his Hu blood and raged, cursing Han: "You Tujue dare thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Lushan heard this as a sneer at his Hu blood and raged, cursing Han: "You Tujue whelp—how dare you!"

sentences.zh: 翰欲應之，力士目翰，翰乃止，陽醉而散，自是爲怨愈深。

translations.literal: Han was about to answer; Lishi signaled Han with his eyes; Han stopped, feigned drunkenness and left—from then hatred ran deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Han was about to retort; Lishi caught his eye; Han held back, pretended drunkenness, and left—and from that day their hatred deepened.

sentences.zh: 棣王琰有二孺人，爭寵，其一使巫書符置琰履中以求媚。

translations.literal: Prince of Di Yan had two junior consorts contending for favor; one had a sorcerer write charms placed in Yan's shoes to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Di Yan had two junior consorts fighting for favor; one had a sorcerer write charms and hide them in Yan's shoes to win him.

sentences.zh: 琰與監院宦者有隙，宦者知之，密奏琰祝詛上；

translations.literal: Yan had a grievance with the supervisory eunuch; the eunuch learned of it and secretly memorialized that Yan cursed the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Yan had fallen out with the supervisory eunuch; the eunuch learned of the charms and secretly reported that Yan cursed the emperor;

sentences.zh: 上使人掩其履而獲之，大怒。

translations.literal: the emperor had his shoes searched and the charms found; he was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor had his shoes searched, found the charms, and flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 琰頓首謝：「臣實不知有符。」

translations.literal: Yan kowtowed: "Your servant truly did not know of the charms."
translations.idiomatic: Yan kowtowed: "Your servant truly knew nothing of the charms."

sentences.zh: 上使鞫之，果孺人所爲。

translations.literal: The emperor had it investigated; it proved to be the junior consort's doing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had it tried; it was indeed the junior consort's work.

sentences.zh: 上猶疑琰知之，囚-{於}-鷹狗坊，絶朝請，憂憤而薨。

translations.literal: The emperor still suspected Yan knew; he imprisoned him in the Hawk and Hound Ward, cut off court attendance; he died of grief and anger.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still suspected Yan had known; he was imprisoned in the Hawk and Hound Ward, barred from court, and died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 故事，兵、吏部尚書知政事者，選事悉委侍郎以下，三注三唱，仍過門下省審，自春及夏，其事乃畢。

translations.literal: By precedent, when Ministers of War and Personnel who knew state affairs handled selection, the affair was entirely delegated below the vice ministers—three nominations, three announcements, still passing the Chancellery for review; from spring to summer the matter was finished.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when the war and personnel ministers who sat in council handled appointments, the work went to vice ministers and below—three lists, three announcements, then review in the Chancellery; from spring to summer the round was done.

sentences.zh: 及楊國忠以宰相領文部尚書，欲自示精敏，乃遣令史先-{於}-私第密定名闕。

translations.literal: When Yang Guozhong as chancellor also held the Ministry of Letters and wished to show himself keen, he sent clerks first to his private house to fix names and vacancies in secret.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong as chancellor also headed the Ministry of Letters and wished to seem sharp, he had clerks fix names and vacancies in secret at his private house first.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬戌，國忠召左相陳希烈及給事中、諸司長官皆集尚書都堂，唱注選人，一日而畢，曰：「今左相、給事中倶在座，已過門下矣。」

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renxu, Guozhong summoned Left Chancellor Chen Xilie and the drafting reviewers and bureau chiefs of every ministry to gather at the Ministry of Letters headquarters, announced appointments for candidates, and finished in a single day, saying, "The left chancellor and drafting reviewers are all seated—this has already passed the Chancellery."
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renxu, Guozhong called Left Chancellor Chen Xilie and the drafting reviewers and bureau chiefs to the Ministry of Letters, read out appointments in one day, and said, "The left chancellor and reviewers are here—this has already cleared the Chancellery."

sentences.zh: 其間資格差繆甚衆，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Among them qualifications were wildly wrong in very many cases; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and seniority were botched in countless cases, and no one dared object.

sentences.zh: -{於}-是門下不-{復}-過官，侍郎但掌試判而已。

translations.literal: From then on the Chancellery no longer passed on offices; vice ministers only handled examination judgments.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Chancellery no longer signed off on posts; vice ministers merely ran the written exams.

sentences.zh: 侍郎韋見素、張倚趨走門庭，與主事無異。

translations.literal: Vice Ministers Wei Jiansu and Zhang Yi hurried through the gates like chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers Wei Jiansu and Zhang Yi scurried through the courtyard gates no differently from chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 見素，湊之子也。

translations.literal: Jiansu was the son of Wei Cou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu was Wei Cou's son.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹鮮-{于}-仲通諷選人請爲國忠刻頌，立-{於}-省門，-{制}-仲通撰其辭；

translations.literal: Jingzhao intendant Xian Yu Zhongtong induced candidates to ask that a eulogy stele be carved for Guozhong and set up at the ministry gate; an edict had Zhongtong compose the text;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao intendant Xian Yu Zhongtong urged candidates to commission a praise stele for Guozhong at the ministry gate; the emperor had Zhongtong draft the inscription;

sentences.zh: 上爲改定數字，仲通以金塡之。

translations.literal: the emperor revised several characters, and Zhongtong inlaid them in gold.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor altered a few characters, and Zhongtong filled them in with gold.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠使人説安祿山誣李林甫與阿布思謀反，祿山使阿布思部落降者詣闕，誣告林甫與阿布思約爲父子。

translations.literal: Guozhong had men persuade An Lushan to accuse Li Linfu of plotting rebellion with Abu Si; Lushan sent surrendered men of Abu Si's tribes to court to denounce Linfu and Abu Si as having sworn father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong had agents tell Lushan to charge Li Linfu with plotting rebellion with Abu Si; Lushan sent surrendered tribesmen of Abu Si to court to claim Linfu and Abu Si had sworn father and son.

sentences.zh: 上信之，下吏按問；

translations.literal: The emperor believed it and handed the case to the judicial officers;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed them and ordered an investigation;

sentences.zh: 林甫婿諫議大夫楊齊宣懼爲所累，附國忠意證成之。

translations.literal: Linfu's son-in-law Remonstrance Officer Yang Qixuan, fearing he would be implicated, sided with Guozhong and helped prove the case.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu's son-in-law Remonstrance Officer Yang Qixuan, afraid of being dragged in, followed Guozhong's line and helped close the case.

sentences.zh: 時林甫尚未葬，二月，癸未，-{制}-削林甫官爵；

translations.literal: Linfu had not yet been buried; in the second month, on guwei, an edict stripped Linfu of rank and titles;
translations.idiomatic: Linfu was still unburied; in the second month, on guwei, an edict stripped him of rank and titles;

sentences.zh: 子孫有官者除名，流嶺南及黔中，給隨身衣及糧食，自-{餘}-資産-{並}-沒官；

translations.literal: descendants who held office were removed from the rolls, exiled to Lingnan and Qianzhong, given traveling clothes and grain; all remaining property was confiscated;
translations.idiomatic: descendants in office were struck from the rolls and banished to Lingnan and Qianzhong with clothes and grain for the road; the rest of their property was seized;

sentences.zh: 近親及黨與坐貶者五十-{餘}-人。

translations.literal: close kin and partisans punished by demotion numbered more than fifty.
translations.idiomatic: more than fifty close kin and associates were demoted with them.

sentences.zh: 剖林甫棺，抉取含珠，褫金紫，更以小棺如庶人禮葬之。

translations.literal: Linfu's coffin was opened, the pearl from his mouth taken, his gold and purple robes stripped, and he was reburied in a small coffin by commoner's rites.
translations.idiomatic: They opened Linfu's coffin, took the pearl from his mouth, stripped his gold and purple, and reburied him in a small coffin with commoner's rites.

sentences.zh: 己亥，賜陳希烈爵許國公，楊國忠爵魏國公，賞其成林甫之獄也。

translations.literal: On jihai, Chen Xilie was given the fief of Duke of Xu and Guozhong the fief of Duke of Wei, rewarding them for completing Linfu's case.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Chen Xilie was made Duke of Xu and Guozhong Duke of Wei, rewarded for finishing Linfu's case.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，己酉，-{復}-以魏、周、隋-{後}-爲三恪，楊國忠欲攻李林甫之短也。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on jiyou, the lines of Wei, Zhou, and Sui were again made the Three Exalted Lines—Guozhong wished to attack Linfu's faults.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on jiyou, the Wei, Zhou, and Sui lines were again made the Three Exalted Lines—Guozhong's blow at Linfu's legacy.

sentences.zh: 衞包以助邪貶夜郎尉，崔昌貶烏雷尉。

translations.literal: Wei Bao was demoted to Ye Lang commandant for aiding evil; Cui Chang was demoted to Wulei commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bao, for aiding evil, was demoted to Ye Lang commandant; Cui Chang to Wulei commandant.

sentences.zh: 阿布思爲回紇所破，安祿山誘其部落而降之，由是祿山精兵，天下莫及。

translations.literal: Abu Si was broken by the Uyghurs; An Lushan enticed his tribes to surrender, and from this Lushan's picked troops had no equal under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Abu Si was shattered by the Uyghurs; Lushan lured his tribes to defect, and from then on his elite army had no match in the empire.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以左武衞大將軍何-{復}-光將嶺南五府兵撃南詔。

translations.literal: On renchen, Left Martial Gate general He Guang was made to lead the five southern circuits' troops against Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Left Martial Gate general He Fuguang was ordered to lead the five southern circuits against Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 安祿山以李林甫狡猾逾己，故畏服之。

translations.literal: An Lushan, because Li Linfu was more cunning than he, therefore feared and obeyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan had feared Linfu, who was craftier than he.

sentences.zh: 及楊國忠爲相，祿山視之蔑如也，由是有隙。

translations.literal: When Yang Guozhong became chancellor, Lushan looked on him with contempt, and from this a rift opened.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guozhong took the seal, Lushan held him in contempt, and the breach between them opened.

sentences.zh: 國忠屢言祿山有反狀，上不-{聽}-。

translations.literal: Guozhong repeatedly said Lushan showed signs of rebellion; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong kept warning that Lushan meant to rebel; the emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度使哥舒翰撃吐蕃，拔洪濟、大漠門等城，悉收九-{曲}-部落。

translations.literal: Longyou commissioner Ge Shuhan attacked the Tibetans, took Hongji, Damen, and other cities, and recovered all the Nine Bends tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou commissioner Ge Shuhan struck Tibet, took Hongji, Damen, and other strongpoints, and recovered the Nine Bends tribes.

sentences.zh: 初，髙麗人王思禮與翰倶爲押牙，事王忠嗣。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Koguryo man Wang Silu and Han had both been yamen teeth and served Wang Zhongsi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Koguryo Wang Silu and Han had both been yamen guards under Wang Zhongsi.

sentences.zh: 翰爲節度使，思禮爲兵馬使兼河源軍使。

translations.literal: When Han became commissioner, Silu was army commander and also commander of the Heyuan army.
translations.idiomatic: When Han became commissioner, Silu was made army commander and Heyuan army commander.

sentences.zh: 翰撃九-{曲}-，思禮-{後}-期；

translations.literal: In the attack on the Nine Bends, Silu was late;
translations.idiomatic: In the Nine Bends campaign Silu was late;

sentences.zh: 翰將斬之，既而-{復}-召釋之。

translations.literal: Han was about to execute him, then called him back and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Han was about to behead him, then recalled him and spared him.

sentences.zh: 思禮徐曰：「斬則遂斬，-{復}-召何爲！」

translations.literal: Silu said calmly, "If you mean to cut off my head, then cut it—why call me back?"
translations.idiomatic: Silu said evenly, "Behead me if you will—why summon me back?"

sentences.zh: 楊國忠欲厚結翰與共排安祿山，奏以翰兼河西節度使。

translations.literal: Guozhong wished to bind Han closely and together push out An Lushan; he memorialized that Han also hold the Hexi commission.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong wanted Han as an ally against Lushan and had him given the Hexi command as well.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，戊戌，賜翰爵西平郡王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on wuxu, Han was given the fief of Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on wuxu, Han was made Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 翰表侍-{御}-史裴冕爲河西行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Han memorialized that Palace Attendant Pei Mian be Hexi acting army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Han recommended Palace Attendant Pei Mian as Hexi acting army commander.

sentences.zh: 是時中國盛強，自安遠門西盡唐境凡萬二千-{里}-，閭閻相望，桑麻翳野，天下稱富庶者無如隴右。

translations.literal: At this time China was mighty; from Anyuan Gate west to the Tang border was twelve thousand li; hamlets faced one another, mulberry and hemp shaded the fields—under heaven none was called richer than Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: China was at its height; from Anyuan Gate west to the frontier ran twelve thousand li of settled country, mulberry and hemp thick on the fields—the wealthiest land in the empire was said to be Longyou.

sentences.zh: 翰毎遣使入奏，常乘白橐駝，日馳五百-{里}-。

translations.literal: Whenever Han sent envoys to memorialize, he would ride a white camel and cover five hundred li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent memorials by white Bactrian camel, five hundred li in a day.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲辰，以突騎施黑姓可汗登裡伊羅蜜施爲突騎施可汗。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiachen, Dengli Yiluomishi of the Black Turgesh was made Turgesh qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiachen, Turgesh Black-Bone qaghan Dengli Yiluomishi was confirmed as Turgesh qaghan.

sentences.zh: 北庭都護程千-{里}-追阿布思至磧西，以書諭葛邏祿，使相應。

translations.literal: Beiting protector Cheng Qianli pursued Abu Si to west of the desert and wrote to the Qarluqs to coordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Beiting protector Cheng Qianli chased Abu Si beyond the sands and wrote the Qarluqs to act in concert.

sentences.zh: 阿布思窮迫，歸葛邏祿，葛邏祿-{葉}-護執之，-{並}-其妻子、麾下數千人送之。

translations.literal: Abu Si, pressed to extremity, fled to the Qarluqs; the Qarluq yabghu seized him and sent him with his wife, children, and several thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: Abu Si, desperate, threw himself on the Qarluqs; their yabghu seized him and sent him on with wife, children, and several thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，加葛邏祿-{葉}-護頓毘伽開府儀同三司，賜爵金山王。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Qarluq yabghu was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the same privileges as the Three Dukes and given the fief of Prince of Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the Qarluq yabghu was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, equal to the Three Dukes, and Prince of Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊寅，上幸華淸宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, the emperor visited Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, the emperor went to Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠與虢國夫人居第相鄰，晝夜往來，無-{復}-期度，或-{並}-轡走馬入朝，不施障幕，道路爲之掩目。

translations.literal: Guozhong and the Lady of Guo lived in neighboring mansions; they came and went day and night without fixed times, sometimes riding side by side to court without screens; the road had to avert its eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong and the Lady of Guo had adjoining houses; they passed back and forth day and night without schedule, sometimes riding abreast to court without screens, and the street had to look away.

sentences.zh: 三夫人將從車駕幸華淸宮，會-{於}-國忠第；

translations.literal: The three ladies were to follow the imperial carriage to Huaqing Palace and met at Guozhong's house;
translations.idiomatic: The three ladies were to join the imperial progress to Huaqing Palace and gathered at Guozhong's mansion;

sentences.zh: 車馬-{僕}-從，充溢數坊，錦繡珠玉，鮮華奪目。

translations.literal: carriages, horses, and attendants filled several wards; brocade, pearls, and jade dazzled the eye.
translations.idiomatic: horses and retinues overflowed several wards; brocade and jewels blazed on every side.

sentences.zh: 國忠謂客曰：「吾本寒家，一旦縁椒房至此，未知稅駕之所，然念終不能致令名，不若且極樂耳。」

translations.literal: Guozhong told guests, "I am from a cold house; in one stroke I rose through the consort clan to this height. I do not know where I shall alight, yet I know I can never win a lasting name—so I may as well take my pleasure to the limit."
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong told guests, "I was born poor; one marriage into the palace clan brought me here. I do not know where I will end, but I know I will never earn a good name—so I might as well enjoy myself while I can."

sentences.zh: 楊氏五家，隊各爲一色衣以相別，五家合隊，粲若-{雲}-錦；

translations.literal: The five Yang houses each dressed their retinues in a single color to distinguish them; when the five joined ranks, the blaze was like clouds of brocade;
translations.idiomatic: The five Yang clans each dressed their columns in one color; together they shone like brocade clouds;

sentences.zh: 國忠仍以劍南旌節引-{於}-其前。

translations.literal: Guozhong still led the way with the Jiannan military banner.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong still marched ahead under the Jiannan commander's banner.

sentences.zh: 國忠子暄舉明經，學業荒陋，不及格。

translations.literal: Guozhong's son Xuan took the classics examination; his learning was crude and he failed.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong's son Xuan sat for the classics exam; his work was wretched and he failed.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎達奚珣畏國忠權勢，遣其子昭應尉撫先白之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Daxi Xun, fearing Guozhong's power, sent his son Fu, Zhaoying commandant, to inform him first.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Daxi Xun, afraid of Guozhong, sent his son Fu, the Zhaoying commandant, to tip him off first.

sentences.zh: 撫伺國忠入朝上馬，趨至馬下；

translations.literal: Fu watched for Guozhong to mount for court and ran to his horse;
translations.idiomatic: Fu caught Guozhong mounting for court and rushed to his stirrup;

sentences.zh: 國忠意其子必中選，有喜色。

translations.literal: Guozhong thought his son would surely pass and looked pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong assumed his son would pass and looked pleased.

sentences.zh: 撫曰：「大人白相公，郎君所試，不中程式，然亦未敢落也。」

translations.literal: Fu said, "My lord told the chief minister that your son's examination did not meet the rules, yet he has not dared fail him."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "My father told the chief minister your son's paper missed the mark, yet he has not dared fail him."

sentences.zh: 國忠怒曰：「我子何患不富貴，乃令鼠輩相賣！」

translations.literal: Guozhong raged: "My son—what worry has he of wealth and honor? You let vermin trade favors!"
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong snapped, "My son need never fear poverty—must mice like you sell favors?"

sentences.zh: 策馬不顧而去。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse away without a backward glance.
translations.idiomatic: He whipped his horse away and never looked back.

sentences.zh: 撫惶遽，書白其父曰：「彼恃挾貴勢，令人慘嗟，安可-{復}-與論-{曲}-直！」

translations.literal: Fu panicked and wrote his father: "He leans on power and rank—it makes one weep; how can we argue right and wrong with him!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu panicked and wrote his father: "He rides his privilege—it breaks the heart; how can we argue justice with him!"

sentences.zh: 遂置暄上第。

translations.literal: Xuan was then placed first in the list.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was placed at the head of the list.

sentences.zh: 及暄爲戸部侍郎，珣始自禮部遷吏部，暄與所親言，猶歎己之淹回，珣之迅疾。

translations.literal: When Xuan became vice minister of revenue, Xun had just moved from Rites to Personnel; Xuan told intimates he still lamented his own slow rise and Xun's swift promotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan became vice minister of revenue, Xun had just left Rites for Personnel; Xuan still complained to friends that he had been held back while Xun rose fast.

sentences.zh: 國忠既居要地，中外餉遺輻湊，積縑至三千萬匹。

translations.literal: Once Guozhong held power, gifts from inside and outside the court poured in; silk alone piled to thirty million bolts.
translations.idiomatic: In high office, gifts from court and country flooded in; plain silk alone stacked to thirty million bolts.

sentences.zh: 上在華淸宮，欲夜出-{遊}-，龍武大將軍陳玄禮諫曰：「宮外即曠野，安可不備不虞！

translations.literal: At Huaqing Palace the emperor wished to go out at night; Dragon Martial general Chen Xuanli remonstrated: "Outside the palace is open country—how can we not guard against the unexpected!
translations.idiomatic: At Huaqing the emperor wanted a night outing; Dragon Martial general Chen Xuanli said, "Beyond the walls is open ground—you cannot go unguarded!

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲夜-{遊}-，請歸城闕。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must go out at night, please return to the city walls."
translations.idiomatic: If you must go out at night, return to the capital."

sentences.zh: 上爲之引還。

translations.literal: The emperor turned back on his account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned back.

sentences.zh: 是歳，安西節度使封常淸撃大勃律，至菩薩勞城，前鋒屢捷，常淸乘勝逐之。

translations.literal: That year, Anxi commissioner Feng Changqing attacked Greater Bolü, reached Bodhisattva Labor City; the vanguard won repeatedly, and Changqing pressed the pursuit in victory.
translations.idiomatic: That year Anxi commissioner Feng Changqing attacked Greater Bolü, reached Bodhisattva Labor City; the van repeatedly won, and Changqing drove the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 斥候府果毅段秀實諫曰：「虜兵羸而屢北，誘我也；

translations.literal: Scout-commander Duan Xiushi of the Fruit-Garrison office remonstrated: "The enemy is weak and retreats again and again—they are baiting us;
translations.idiomatic: Scout officer Duan Xiushi warned, "The foe is weak and keeps falling back—they are baiting us;

sentences.zh: 請搜左右山林。」

translations.literal: please search the hills and woods on both flanks."
translations.idiomatic: search the woods on both sides."

sentences.zh: 常淸從之，果獲伏兵，遂大破之，受降而還。

translations.literal: Changqing followed his advice, indeed found ambush troops, utterly defeated them, accepted their surrender, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing listened, found the ambush, routed them utterly, took their surrender, and returned.

sentences.zh: 中書-{舍}-人宋昱知選事，前進士廣平劉乃以選法未善，上書-{於}-昱，以爲：「禹、稷、皋陶同居舜朝，猶曰載采有九德，考績以九載。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafting Officer Song Yu knew selection affairs; former metropolitan candidate Liu Nai of Guangping, because the selection law was not good, memorialized Yu, holding that: "Yu, Ji, and Gao Yao served together in Shun's court, yet they still said to employ the nine virtues and examine merit over nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Officer Song Yu ran appointments; former candidate Liu Nai of Guangping, finding the law unsound, wrote Yu that "even Yu, Ji, and Gao Yao in Shun's court still spoke of the nine virtues and nine years of review.

sentences.zh: 近代主司，察言-{於}-一幅之判，觀行-{於}-一揖之間，何古今遲速不侔之甚哉！

translations.literal: Modern examiners judge words in a single sheet of judgment and conduct in a single bow—how unlike ancient and modern in speed and slowness!
translations.idiomatic: Today's masters read one exam sheet and one bow—how unlike the ancients in pace!

sentences.zh: 借使周公、孔子今處銓廷，考其辭華，則不及徐、庾，觀其利口，則不若嗇夫，何暇論聖賢之事業乎！」

translations.literal: Suppose the Duke of Zhou and Confucius now sat in the Selection Bureau: test their literary grace and they would fall short of Xu and Yu; watch their sharp tongues and they would not match the tax clerk—when would there be time to discuss the careers of sages!"
translations.idiomatic: Put the Duke of Zhou and Confucius in the Board today: their prose would lose to Xu and Yu, their tongues to a petty clerk—who would speak of sage's work?"
